entries.definitionCN: 以基本或元素的方式；带着自然力的强度。

entries.definition: a part of a machine or system that can be identified separately. It is more mechanical than element.
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统中可单独识别的部分。它比 element 更机械。

entries.definition: one of the things that influences a result. It fits the 'element of surprise' sense better than a physical part.
entries.definitionCN: 影响结果的因素之一。它比“物理部分”更贴合 element of surprise 这一义。

entries.definition: one of the parts that make up a whole, especially in a formal or technical description.
entries.definitionCN: 构成整体的部分之一，尤用于正式或技术描述。

entries.definition: one of the substances mixed to make something, especially food. It implies blending, while element implies building.
entries.definitionCN: 混合制成某物（尤指食物）的物质之一。它含“混合”义，element 含“构成”义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin elementum 'first principle', the pair elemental/elementary, and compounds like heating element and trace element.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 elementum“第一原理”、elemental/elementary 这一对，以及 heating element、trace element 等复合词。

normal.en: An element is the smallest block you cannot break any further without losing the thing.
normal.cn: element 是你再拆就会失去这个东西的最小积木。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the strict sense: one kind of atom, listed on the periodic table.
normal.cn: 化学保留最严格的义项：一种原子，列在周期表上。

normal.en: Elemental means raw and natural; elementary means beginner-level. Keep them apart.
normal.cn: elemental 是原始、自然力的；elementary 是入门级的。要把两者分开。

normal.en: In one's element: back in the medium you were made for, like a fish in water.
normal.cn: in one's element：回到你天生所属的介质里，像鱼在水里。

normal.en: A heating element is simply one functional part of a whole appliance.
normal.cn: 加热元件不过是一台电器整体中的一个功能部件。

abstract.en: Every whole is a lie until you can name its elements.
abstract.cn: 在你能说清它的元素之前，每个整体都是一句谎话。

abstract.en: An element is a part that does not know it is being analysed.
abstract.cn: 元素是一个不知道自己正被分析的部分。

abstract.en: To be in your element is to stop translating yourself.
abstract.cn: 如鱼得水，就是不再需要翻译自己。

examples.en: Iron is an element, while rust is a compound of iron and oxygen.
examples.cn: 铁是元素，而铁锈是铁与氧的化合物。

examples.en: Timing is a key element in a successful apology.
examples.cn: 时机是一次成功道歉的关键要素。

examples.en: The tent gave them some protection from the elements.
examples.cn: 帐篷为他们提供了一些抵御风雨的保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱立门特”——爱立门特把门拆到最小一颗颗零件，发现再也拆不动 → element 元素、要素

root: 源自拉丁语 elementum“第一原理、基础”，也指四元素与字母；更深来源不确定。核心是“构成整体的最小单位，或一个人所属的自然介质”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of element, all circling one idea: the smallest part out of which a whole is built, or the medium a thing naturally belongs to.
sensesIntro.cn: element 的九个义项都围绕一个观念：构成整体的最小部分，或某物天然所属的介质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the smallest blocks in a pile, the ones you cannot split without destroying the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆里最小的那几块积木，再拆就会毁掉这个东西。

branches.en: BUILDING BLOCKS: atoms, set members, and device components are all smallest units of a larger structure.
branches.cn: 构件：原子、集合成员、器件，都是更大结构中的最小单位。

branches.en: PARTS OF A WHOLE: a plan, a situation, and a work of art can each be analysed into elements.
branches.cn: 整体的部分：计划、局面与艺术品，都能被分析成若干要素。

branches.en: HABITAT: the classical element a creature belongs to becomes its natural environment and comfort zone.
branches.cn: 栖息：生物所属的古典元素，化为它的自然环境与舒适区。

branches.en: FORCE: the same four elements, out of balance, become violent weather and human wrath.
branches.cn: 力量：同样四种元素一旦失衡，就成了狂暴天气与人的怒火。

branches.en: ALPHABET: the elements of a subject are its first letters, learned before anything else.
branches.cn: 字母表：一门学问的 elements 就是它的入门字母，最先学。

intro.en: Element's family is small and easy to confuse. Elemental refers to raw natural force; elementary refers to first principles. Compounds like multi-element and trace element are transparent.
intro.cn: element 的词族不大，却容易混。elemental 指原始自然力；elementary 指最初原理。multi-element、trace element 等复合词则一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun is elementum, of uncertain deeper origin. It is the only reliable classical form, so latinEntries records it without inventing a root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词是 elementum，更深来源不确定。它是唯一可靠的古典形式，因此 latinEntries 只记录它，不编造词根。

items.meaning: relating to the elements or to raw natural force
items.meaningCN: 与元素或原始自然力有关的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The storm released an elemental force against the coast.
items.exampleCN: 风暴向海岸释放出一种原始的自然力。

items.meaning: concerned with first principles; introductory
items.meaningCN: 关于基本原理的；入门的（-ary 构成形容词）
items.example: The book explains elementary physics without mathematics.
items.exampleCN: 这本书不用数学解释基础物理。

items.meaning: in a basic or elemental manner
items.meaningCN: 以基本或元素的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The landscape is elementally simple: rock, sky, and sea.
items.exampleCN: 这片风景在元素上极简：岩石、天空与海。

items.meaning: made of or involving several elements
items.meaningCN: 多元素的；涉及多个要素的（multi- 表示“多”）
items.example: The sensor is a multi-element array that detects direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个传感器是多元件阵列，能探测方向。

items.meaning: one element at a time, in mathematics and computing
items.meaningCN: 逐元素的；在数学与计算中一次处理一个元素
items.example: The program adds the two arrays elementwise.
items.exampleCN: 程序逐元素相加这两个数组。

items.meaning: a smaller element within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 更大元素内部的子元素（sub- 表示“在下”）
items.example: Each XML element may contain several subelements.
items.exampleCN: 每个 XML 元素可以包含若干子元素。

items.meaning: the part of a device that produces heat
items.meaningCN: 电器中产生热量的部件（复合名词）
items.example: The heating element glows red when the oven is on.
items.exampleCN: 烤箱开着时，加热元件发红。

items.meaning: a chemical element needed or present only in tiny amounts
items.meaningCN: 只需微量或仅微量存在的化学元素
items.example: Zinc is a trace element essential to many enzymes.
items.exampleCN: 锌是许多酶必需的微量元素。

items.meaning: one of a group of metallic elements used in magnets and electronics
items.meaningCN: 用于磁体与电子器件的一组金属元素
items.example: The motor depends on rare-earth elements such as neodymium.
items.exampleCN: 这种电机依赖钕等稀土元素。

items.meaning: the advantage gained by acting unexpectedly
items.meaningCN: 因出其不意而获得的优势（固定短语）
items.example: The night attack relied on the element of surprise.
items.exampleCN: 夜袭依靠的就是出其不意。

definition_zh: 消除；清除；淘汰；排除；排泄；消灭
definition_en: to remove something completely, to exclude it from consideration, or to put someone out of a competition
core_image: 把东西推到门槛外面：门一关，屋里就没有它了。
scene: The team was eliminated in the first round after losing both matches.
sceneCN: 这里 eliminate 是「淘汰出局、从名单上划掉」（第 2 个义项：竞赛淘汰）；句意：这支队伍两场皆负，首轮即被淘汰。场景要点：赛程表上被划掉的一行、空着的下一轮格子。

pos.zh: 消除；淘汰；排除；排泄；消灭

derivatives.zh: 消除性的；倾向于排除的
消除者；淘汰赛；消除装置

senses.title: Remove a physical object entirely
senses.titleCN: 清出实物：让屋里没有它
senses.definition: to remove a physical thing completely so that it is no longer present
senses.definitionCN: 把某个实物彻底移走，使它不再存在于原处
senses.example: Workers eliminated every trace of the oil spill from the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 工人清除了沙滩上泄漏原油的全部痕迹。
senses.why: The Latin phrase was ex limine, 'off the threshold'. The first picture is an object pushed out through the doorway, so the room behind the door is clean.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语是 ex limine“离开门槛”。最初的画面是把东西从门口推出去，于是门后的屋子就干净了。

senses.title: Knock a team out of a competition
senses.titleCN: 竞赛淘汰：从赛程上划掉
senses.definition: to defeat a player or team so that they take no further part in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 击败选手或队伍，使其不再参加后续比赛
senses.example: The defending champions were eliminated in the quarter-finals.
senses.exampleCN: 卫冕冠军在四分之一决赛中被淘汰。
senses.why: The tournament list is the 'house'; a beaten team is pushed out of that list. Elimination here is administrative removal, not physical destruction.
senses.whyCN: 赛程表就是那间“屋子”；输掉的队被推出这张名单。这里的淘汰是名单上的移除，而不是物理上的毁灭。

senses.title: Rule something out of consideration
senses.titleCN: 排除可能：它不在考虑范围
senses.definition: to show that something is not possible or not the cause, so it need not be considered
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事不可能或不是原因，因此无须再考虑
senses.example: The doctor eliminated several rare conditions before ordering more tests.
senses.exampleCN: 医生先排除了几种罕见病，才安排进一步检查。
senses.why: Reasoning is pictured as a set of candidates standing in a room. Each elimination removes one candidate from the room until only one is left standing.
senses.whyCN: 推理被想成一群候选者站在屋里。每排除一个，就是从屋里移走一个，直到只剩一个站着。

senses.title: Expel waste from the body
senses.titleCN: 排泄：身体把废物送出门
senses.definition: to get rid of waste substances from the body, especially through the kidneys or intestines
senses.definitionCN: 把体内废物排出体外，尤指通过肾脏或肠道
senses.example: The kidneys eliminate excess salt and water as urine.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏把多余的盐和水以尿液形式排出。
senses.why: The body is the enclosed space and the waste is the object pushed out past its threshold. This medical sense is recorded from about 1795.
senses.whyCN: 身体是被围起来的空间，废物就是被推过门槛送出去的东西。这个医学义约在 1795 年见于记录。

senses.title: Kill or remove a person
senses.titleCN: 除掉某人：委婉说法
senses.definition: to kill someone, or to remove a person as a threat, often used as a euphemism
senses.definitionCN: 杀死某人，或把某人当作威胁清除掉，常用作委婉说法
senses.example: The regime eliminated its political opponents one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权逐个除掉了政敌。
senses.why: Here the object pushed out of the house is a person, and the clean room is a world without that person. The euphemism softens the same physical gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这里被推出屋子的对象是人，“干净的屋子”就是没有这个人的世界。委婉说法把同一个物理动作说轻了。

senses.title: Mathematics: remove a variable
senses.titleCN: 数学消元：把未知数去掉
senses.definition: in algebra, to remove a variable or term by combining equations, so that one unknown disappears
senses.definitionCN: 在代数中通过合并方程消去某个变量或项，使一个未知数消失
senses.example: Add the two equations to eliminate x.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个方程相加，消去 x。
senses.why: The equation is a container holding several unknowns. Combining two equations pushes one unknown out of the container, leaving a simpler problem.
senses.whyCN: 方程是装着若干未知数的容器。合并两个方程就是把其中一个未知数推出容器，留下更简单的问题。

senses.title: Eradicate a problem at its source
senses.titleCN: 根除问题：从源头消除
senses.definition: to remove the cause of a problem so completely that it cannot recur
senses.definitionCN: 彻底去掉问题的成因，使其无法再发生
senses.example: Vaccination has eliminated smallpox from the world.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗接种已在全球根除了天花。
senses.why: Removing every infected case, not just every visible symptom, leaves the house empty enough that the thing cannot move back in.
senses.whyCN: 清除每一个感染病例而不只是可见症状，才让屋子空到它搬不回来。

senses.title: Sports: wipe out a deficit
senses.titleCN: 体育抹平差距：把落后数清零
senses.definition: in sport, to cancel out a lead so that the score is level again
senses.definitionCN: 在体育比赛中把对方的领先优势抵消掉，使比分重新持平
senses.example: Two late goals eliminated a three-point deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 终场前的两个进球抹平了三分之差。
senses.why: The deficit is a number standing between the teams; scoring makes it disappear from the scoreboard, exactly like an object taken off a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 分差是立在两队之间的一个数字；进球让它从记分牌上消失，就像从架子上拿走一件东西。

senses.title: Make something unnecessary
senses.titleCN: 使不再需要：把需求自身消除
senses.definition: to make a step, cost, or difficulty no longer needed
senses.definitionCN: 使某个步骤、成本或困难不再必要
senses.example: Digital tickets eliminated the need to queue at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 电子票省去了在门口排队的需求。
senses.why: What is eliminated here is not a thing but the need for a thing. Once the need is pushed out, the whole step disappears from the plan.
senses.whyCN: 这里被消除的不是某物，而是对某物的“需要”。需要一被推出门，整个步骤就从计划里消失了。

intro.en: Eliminate is a Latin phrase frozen into a verb: ex limine, 'off the threshold'. Everything it means today grows from the act of pushing something out through a door.
intro.cn: eliminate 是一个凝固成动词的拉丁短语：ex limine“离开门槛”。它今天的所有意思，都从“把东西从门口推出去”这个动作长出来。

items.en: Limen meant 'threshold', the strip of ground you cross to enter a house. It is also the likely relative of limes 'boundary, border', the source of English limit.
items.cn: limen 意为“门槛”，即进屋时要跨过的那条地面。它很可能与 limes“边界、国界”同族，而 limes 是英语 limit 的来源。

items.en: The phrase ex limine meant 'off the threshold', that is, outside the door. It was said of a person or thing driven out of the house.
items.cn: 短语 ex limine 意为“离开门槛”，也就是门外。用于被赶出屋子的人或物。

items.en: From the phrase came the verb eliminare 'to thrust out of doors, expel'. Its past participle eliminatus is the form English took over.
items.cn: 由这个短语产生了动词 eliminare“推出门外、驱逐”。英语直接承接的是它的过去分词 eliminatus。

items.en: Eliminate enters English in the 1560s meaning 'to thrust out, remove, throw out of doors'. The earliest uses are literal: something is physically put out.
items.cn: eliminate 于 16 世纪 60 年代进入英语，意为“推出、移走、扔出门外”。最早的用法是字面的：某物被实际搬到外面。

items.en: The sense 'exclude, set aside as undesirable' is recorded by 1714; 'expel waste from the body' by about 1795. Removal moves from objects to ideas and to the body.
items.cn: “排除、作为不必要之物弃置”的义项 1714 年见于记录；“把废物排出体外”约在 1795 年。移除的对象从物件扩展到观念和身体。

items.en: Algebra, sport, public health, and engineering all use the word for making something disappear from a set or a system. The threshold is now any boundary.
items.cn: 代数、体育、公共卫生和工程都用这个词表示“让某物从集合或系统中消失”。门槛如今可以是任何一条边界。

note.en: The first group shares the limen 'threshold' family or is built directly on eliminate; the second collects words for removal, each with a different force.
note.cn: 第一组共享 limen“门槛”词族，或直接由 eliminate 构成；第二组收“移除”类近义词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: a boundary or the greatest amount allowed. It comes from Latin limes 'boundary', a close relative of limen 'threshold'.
entries.definitionCN: 界限；允许的最大量。它来自拉丁语 limes“边界”，与 limen“门槛”是同族近亲。

entries.definition: the act of removing or excluding something, or the body's removal of waste. It is the noun of eliminate, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 消除、排除的行为，或身体的排泄。它是 eliminate 的名词派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: able to be removed or ruled out. It adds -able to the verb stem.
entries.definitionCN: 可被消除或排除的。它把 -able 加在动词词干上。

entries.definition: to mark the boundary of something. De- 'down, fully' + limitare from limes 'boundary'; it marks a line rather than removing what is inside.
entries.definitionCN: 划定某物的边界。de-“向下、完全”+ 来自 limes“边界”的 limitare；它是画线，而不是清空线内之物。

entries.definition: to take something away from a place. It is the neutral word; eliminate adds the idea that nothing is left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某处拿走。它是最中性的词；eliminate 多了“一点不剩”的意思。

entries.definition: to destroy something completely, literally 'pull up by the roots'. It is stronger and more often used of disease, poverty, or weeds.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底消灭，字面是“连根拔起”。它语气更强，多用于疾病、贫困或杂草。

entries.definition: to keep someone or something out of a group or place. It stresses the barrier; eliminate stresses the removal.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物挡在群体或场所之外。它强调屏障；eliminate 强调移除。

entries.definition: to force someone or something out, often officially. It keeps the physical pushing image that eliminate has lost.
entries.definitionCN: 用力把某人或某物赶出去，常含官方意味。它保留了 eliminate 已经淡化的“推出去”画面。

entries.definition: to end a law, system, or practice officially. It applies to rules and institutions, while eliminate applies to anything removable.
entries.definitionCN: 正式废止法律、制度或惯例。它用于规则与制度，而 eliminate 可用于任何可移除之物。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin ex 'out' + limen 'threshold', giving eliminare 'thrust out of doors'; family words elimination, eliminative, eliminatory, eliminator, eliminable.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 ex“出”+ limen“门槛”，合成 eliminare“推出门外”；词族为 elimination、eliminative、eliminatory、eliminator、eliminable。

normal.en: Picture a doorman pushing a crate over the threshold: ex limine is exactly 'off the threshold'.
normal.cn: 想象门房把一只箱子推过门槛：ex limine 正是“离开门槛”。

normal.en: Limit and eliminate are relatives: limes is the border line, limen is the threshold you cross.
normal.cn: limit 与 eliminate 是同族：limes 是边界线，limen 是你跨过的门槛。

normal.en: In algebra you push x out of the equation; in a tournament you push a team out of the draw. Same door.
normal.cn: 代数里把 x 推出方程；淘汰赛里把球队推出签表。同一扇门。

normal.en: The body eliminates waste the same way a house removes rubbish — over the threshold and out.
normal.cn: 身体排泄废物就像屋子清垃圾——过门槛，出去。

normal.en: Process of elimination works because each candidate you push out leaves the room emptier.
normal.cn: 排除法之所以有效，是因为每推出去一个候选者，屋子就空一分。

abstract.en: Elimination is not the opposite of creation; it is how a system decides what it will be.
abstract.cn: 消除不是创造的反面，而是一个系统决定“自己要成为什么”的方式。

abstract.en: What you can rule out defines the shape of what remains.
abstract.cn: 你能排除什么，决定了剩下之物的形状。

abstract.en: A clean room is not an empty one; it is one where everything left has earned its place.
abstract.cn: 干净的屋子不是空屋子，而是留下的每样东西都配得上它的位置。

examples.en: The new filter eliminates almost all of the fine dust from the air.
examples.cn: 新滤网能清除空气中几乎全部细尘。

examples.en: Investigators eliminated the possibility of a gas leak before the building reopened.
examples.cn: 在大楼重新开放前，调查人员排除了燃气泄漏的可能。

examples.en: The vaccine campaign aimed to eliminate the disease from the region by 2030.
examples.cn: 这场疫苗接种行动的目标是到 2030 年在该地区根除这种疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一粒米捏他”——把最后一粒米都捏出来扔到门槛外，一粒不剩 → eliminate 清除、淘汰

root: 源自拉丁语 ex limine“从门槛出去”，由 ex“出”+ limen“门槛”构成，动词 eliminare 字面是“推到门外”；核心是“清出门外、一点不留”。limen 与 limes“边界”（英语 limit 的来源）同族。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of eliminate, all one gesture: something is pushed past a boundary, and the space inside is left without it.
sensesIntro.cn: eliminate 的九个义项是同一个动作：把某物推过一条边界，里面的空间就不再有其存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway with a threshold; a hand pushes something across it and shuts the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道带门槛的门；一只手把东西推过门槛，然后关上门。

branches.en: BODY AND THINGS: objects and bodily waste both leave through a physical opening; the medical sense dates from about 1795.
branches.cn: 物体与身体：物件和体内废物都从物理开口离开；医学义约始于 1795 年。

branches.en: COMPETITION: a team is struck from the draw, a deficit is struck from the scoreboard — removal done on paper or on a board.
branches.cn: 竞赛：球队从签表上被划掉，分差从记分牌上被划掉——都是在纸面或牌面上的移除。

branches.en: REASONING: candidates in an argument and variables in an equation are both removed from a set until only the answer is left.
branches.cn: 推理：论证中的候选者与方程中的变量，都是从集合里被移走，直到只剩答案。

branches.en: PERSONS: the same pushing gesture applied to a human being becomes a euphemism for killing.
branches.cn: 人：同一个推出动作用在人身上，就成了“除掉”的委婉说法。

branches.en: PREVENTION: remove the cause, or remove the need, and the thing can never come back through the door.
branches.cn: 预防：去掉成因，或去掉需求，那东西就再也进不了这扇门。

intro.en: Eliminate's family is built on the Latin verb eliminare and its participle eliminatus. The suffixes mark the act, the tendency, the purpose, the agent, and the possibility of removal.
intro.cn: eliminate 的词族建立在拉丁动词 eliminare 及其分词 eliminatus 上。后缀分别标记行为、倾向、用途、施事与“可被移除”的可能。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are limen 'threshold', the phrase ex limine, the verb eliminare, and eliminatus. Limes 'boundary' is probably related and yields limit, but the exact link is stated as probable rather than certain.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 limen“门槛”、短语 ex limine、动词 eliminare 与分词 eliminatus。limes“边界”很可能同族并衍生出 limit，但其确切关系只标为“很可能”，并非确证。

items.meaning: the act of removing, excluding, or expelling waste
items.meaningCN: 消除、排除或排泄的行为（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The elimination of tariffs lowered prices.
items.exampleCN: 取消关税使价格下降。

items.meaning: tending to remove or exclude
items.meaningCN: 倾向于消除或排除的（-ive 构成倾向形容词）
items.example: The committee took an eliminative approach, cutting candidates early.
items.exampleCN: 委员会采取淘汰式做法，很早就砍掉候选者。

items.meaning: serving to eliminate, especially as a stage
items.meaningCN: 用于消除的，尤指作为淘汰阶段的（-ory 构成用途形容词）
items.example: The first round is eliminatory; only eight teams advance.
items.exampleCN: 首轮是淘汰性的，只有八支队伍晋级。

items.meaning: one who or that which eliminates; also a knockout match
items.meaningCN: 消除者或消除装置；也指淘汰赛（-or 构成施事名词）
items.example: The device is a stain eliminator for hospital laundry.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备是医院洗衣用的去渍装置。

items.meaning: able to be removed or ruled out
items.meaningCN: 可被消除或排除的（-able 构成能力形容词）
items.example: The error is eliminable with a single check.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误只要一次检查就能消除。

items.meaning: that cannot be removed or ruled out
items.meaningCN: 无法消除或排除的（in- 表示否定）
items.example: Some uncertainty is ineliminable in field research.
items.exampleCN: 田野研究中有些不确定性无法消除。

items.meaning: to remove someone or something from a group, list, or body
items.meaningCN: 从群体、名单或机构中移除（from 标记来源）
items.example: The drug was eliminated from the list of approved treatments.
items.exampleCN: 该药被从获批治疗清单中删除。

items.meaning: the method of ruling out candidates one by one to reach the answer
items.meaningCN: 逐个排除候选者以得到答案的方法
items.example: By process of elimination, the fault is in the last cable.
items.exampleCN: 用排除法可知，故障在最后一根线缆上。

items.meaning: a stage in which losers leave the competition
items.meaningCN: 败者离场的淘汰轮次
items.example: They survived three elimination rounds.
items.exampleCN: 他们挺过了三轮淘汰赛。

items.meaning: a diet that removes suspected foods to identify an allergy
items.meaningCN: 去掉可疑食物以查明过敏原的饮食方案
items.example: The doctor suggested an elimination diet for two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 医生建议进行两周的排除性饮食。

latinEntries.meaning: to thrust out of doors, expel
boundary, border line; probably related to limen
latinEntries.meaningCN: 边界；界线；很可能与 limen 同族

definition_zh: 浮现；出现；显露；兴起；脱颖而出
definition_en: to come up out of a liquid or hiding place, to become visible or known, or to come into existence
core_image: 一个东西从水面下慢慢浮上来，破水而出。
scene: A dolphin emerged from the dark water beside the boat and blew a column of spray.
sceneCN: 这里 emerge 是「从水面下浮出、破水而出」（第 1 个义项：浮出液体）；句意：一头海豚从船边的深水里浮出，喷出一道水柱。场景要点：水面、破水而出的背脊、水雾。

pos.zh: 浮现；出现；显露；兴起；摆脱困境

derivatives.zh: 新兴的； emergent 的；涌现的
紧急情况；突发事件（同源，义已分化）

senses.title: Rise out of a liquid
senses.titleCN: 浮出水面：靠浮力升起
senses.definition: to come up out of water or another liquid and break the surface
senses.definitionCN: 从水或其他液体中升上来并冲破液面
senses.example: The submarine emerged slowly, bow first.
senses.exampleCN: 潜艇缓缓浮出水面，艇首在前。
senses.why: Latin emergere is ex 'out' + mergere 'to dip, sink'. The original picture is buoyancy: a body that was sunk comes back up through the surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 emergere 是 ex“出”+ mergere“浸、沉”。最初的画面是浮力：沉下去的东西又从液面冒回来。

senses.title: Come out of a hiding place
senses.titleCN: 从藏身处出来：不再被遮住
senses.definition: to come out from behind or under something that concealed you
senses.definitionCN: 从遮蔽你的东西后面或下面出来
senses.example: The fox emerged from the bushes only after the dogs had gone.
senses.exampleCN: 狗走远之后，狐狸才从灌木丛里出来。
senses.why: The covering is treated as a liquid-like medium: whatever is hidden in it rises out and stands clear of it.
senses.whyCN: 遮蔽物被当成一种类似液体的介质：藏在里面的东西从中升起，站到它之外。

senses.title: Appear on the scene
senses.titleCN: 现身登场：进入视野
senses.definition: to appear in a place or situation, often after being absent
senses.definitionCN: 出现在某处或某种局面中，常指此前不在
senses.example: A figure emerged from the fog at the end of the pier.
senses.exampleCN: 一个人影从码头尽头的雾里现身。
senses.why: Once something has risen above its medium, it is visible. The physical surfacing becomes the general act of appearing.
senses.whyCN: 某物一旦升到介质之上，就看得见了。物理上的“浮出”由此变成一般的“出现”。

senses.title: Become known as a fact
senses.titleCN: 真相显露：从暗处浮上来
senses.definition: of information, to become known, especially after being hidden or unclear
senses.definitionCN: 指信息被人知道，尤指原本被隐瞒或不清楚之事
senses.example: It later emerged that the report had been altered.
senses.exampleCN: 后来才知道，那份报告被改动过。
senses.why: Facts that were buried in darkness rise into the light. The grammar it emerged that marks this impersonal surfacing of truth.
senses.whyCN: 埋在暗处的事实升到光里。it emerged that 这个句式标记的正是真相这种“非人称的浮出”。

senses.title: Come into existence
senses.titleCN: 事物兴起：从无到有
senses.definition: to begin to exist or to develop, especially as a new pattern or group
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在或发展，尤指新的模式或群体
senses.example: A new middle class emerged in the coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海城市出现了一个新的中产阶层。
senses.why: What did not exist is pictured as sunk below the level of the visible; when conditions change it rises into being. Existence becomes a surface.
senses.whyCN: 尚不存在之物被想象为沉在可见平面之下；条件一变，它就升入存在。存在本身成了一道水面。

senses.title: Get out of a difficult period
senses.titleCN: 走出困境：从深处升回地面
senses.definition: to come out of a war, crisis, or difficult condition, usually in a changed state
senses.definitionCN: 从战争、危机或困境中走出来，通常已换了状态
senses.example: The country emerged from the war with a stronger economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家从战争中走出来时，经济更强了。
senses.why: A crisis is deep water. Emerging is rising back to the surface, and the direction of the verb implies relief as well as exit.
senses.whyCN: 危机是深水。emerge 是重新升回水面，这个方向本身就带出“脱离”与“松一口气”的意思。

senses.title: Come out on top in a contest
senses.titleCN: 脱颖而出：从人群里站到最前
senses.definition: to end a contest or comparison as the winner or the strongest
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛或比较中最终成为胜者或最强者
senses.example: She emerged as the clear leader of the movement.
senses.exampleCN: 她脱颖而出，成为这场运动明确的领袖。
senses.why: In a crowd, most figures stay at the same level; the one who rises above it becomes visible as the leader. The surface is now social.
senses.whyCN: 在人群里，多数人都停在同一高度；升到平面之上的人，就成了看得见的领袖。这道水面如今是社会的。

senses.title: Of a plant: break through the soil
senses.titleCN: 植物破土：芽顶出土面
senses.definition: of a seedling or shoot, to push up through the soil and appear
senses.definitionCN: 指幼苗或新芽顶开土壤、露出地面
senses.example: The first shoots emerged three weeks after planting.
senses.exampleCN: 播种三周后，第一批新芽破土而出。
senses.why: Soil works like a dark liquid: the shoot is buried, then rises and crosses the surface. This is the literal image applied to growth.
senses.whyCN: 土壤就像深色的液体：嫩芽埋在里面，然后升起、越过表面。这是“浮出”画面在生长上的字面用法。

senses.title: Systems: properties that arise from parts
senses.titleCN: 系统涌现：整体生出部分没有的性质
senses.definition: of a property or behaviour, to arise from the interaction of simpler parts rather than from any one part
senses.definitionCN: 指某种性质或行为由更简单的部分相互作用而生，而非来自任何单个部分
senses.example: Consciousness is said to emerge from the activity of many neurons.
senses.exampleCN: 一般认为，意识由大量神经元的活动涌现而来。
senses.why: Nothing at the lower level contains the new property; it appears at the higher level. The word keeps the picture of something rising from a medium it was not visible in.
senses.whyCN: 低层没有任何一个部分含有这种新性质，它出现在高层。这个词保留了“从看不见它的介质中升起”的画面。

intro.en: Emerge is Latin ex 'out' + mergere 'to sink', borrowed through French. The whole family is built on the image of a body rising from water.
intro.cn: emerge 是拉丁语 ex“出”+ mergere“沉”，经法语借入。整个词族都建立在“身体从水中升起”这个画面上。

items.en: Mergere meant 'to dip, plunge, immerse, sink'. It is probably a rhotacised form of *mezgo, from PIE *mezgo- 'to dip, sink, wash'.
items.cn: mergere 意为“浸、插入、沉入”。它很可能是 *mezgo 经过 r 音变而来，源头是原始印欧语 *mezgo-“浸、沉、洗”。

items.en: Emergere combined ex 'out, up out of' with mergere: 'to rise out or up, come forth, come up'. The notion, as standard references put it, is rising from a liquid by virtue of buoyancy.
items.cn: emergere 把 ex“出、从……中升起”与 mergere 结合：“升出、冒出、升起”。通行资料的说明是：靠浮力从液体中升起。

items.en: French émerger carried the same sense. English took the verb from French and also directly from Latin emergere.
items.cn: 法语 émerger 承载同一含义。英语既从法语借入这个动词，也直接取自拉丁语 emergere。

items.en: Recorded in English in the 1560s with the full sense 'to rise from or out of anything that surrounds, covers, or conceals; come forth; appear'.
items.cn: 16 世纪 60 年代见于英语，义项完整：“从环绕、覆盖或遮蔽它的东西中升起或出来；冒出；出现”。

items.en: Emergence (1640s) first meant an unforeseen occurrence, the sense now carried by emergency. The 'coming forth from obscurity' sense is attested by 1704 and general by 1755.
items.cn: emergence（17 世纪 40 年代）最初指“未能预见的事件”，即今天 emergency 承担的意思。“从隐晦中显现”的义项 1704 年见于记录，1755 年已通用。

items.en: Newspaper reporting made it emerged that a fixed phrase; science uses emergence for properties of a whole that none of its parts has.
items.cn: 新闻报道使 it emerged that 成为固定句式；科学则用 emergence 指整体具有而任何部分都没有的性质。

note.en: The first group shares the mergere root, including words that sink in the opposite direction; the second collects verbs of appearing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mergere 词根，包括朝相反方向“沉下去”的词；第二组收“出现”类动词。

entries.definition: to combine into one. It comes from Latin mergere 'to dip, sink', the same verb that gives emerge its second half.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一体。它来自拉丁语 mergere“浸、沉”，也就是构成 emerge 后半部的同一个动词。

entries.definition: the process of coming forth or appearing. Its oldest English sense was 'unforeseen event', now carried by emergency.
entries.definitionCN: 出现、显现的过程。它最早的英语义是“未预见的事件”，如今由 emergency 承担。

entries.definition: a sudden dangerous situation needing immediate action. It began as 'something that emerges unexpectedly', not as a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的突发危险局面。它最初指“意外冒出的事”，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: to put under water or sink below a surface. Sub- 'under' + mergere 'sink' is the exact mirror of emerge.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放到水下或沉到表面之下。sub-“在下”+ mergere“沉”，正好是 emerge 的镜像。

entries.definition: to become visible or present. It is the plain neutral word; emerge suggests coming out of something that covered or hid you.
entries.definitionCN: 变得可见或到场。它是最朴素中性的词；emerge 暗示从覆盖或遮蔽你的东西里出来。

entries.definition: to begin to exist, especially of problems or situations. It matches emerge in the 'come into existence' sense but is more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 开始存在，多用于问题或局面。它在“事物兴起”义上与 emerge 相合，但更正式。

entries.definition: to come up to the surface, or of information, to become known. It keeps the water image openly, where emerge has generalized it.
entries.definitionCN: 升到表面；指信息显露。它明着保留水面意象，而 emerge 已把它泛化。

entries.definition: to appear suddenly in a place, often as if from nothing. It adds surprise; emerge does not require it.
entries.definitionCN: 突然在某处出现，常带“凭空而来”的意味。它多了意外感，而 emerge 不要求这层意思。

entries.definition: to leave a place or become known. It is the everyday equivalent of emerge and carries no Latin weight.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某处；或被人知道。它是 emerge 的日常说法，不带拉丁语的分量。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin ex 'out' + mergere 'sink', giving emergere 'rise out of'; family words emergence, emergent, emergency, submerge, merge.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 ex“出”+ mergere“沉”，合成 emergere“从……中升起”；词族为 emergence、emergent、emergency、submerge、merge。

normal.en: Emerge and submerge are the same verb with opposite prefixes: out of the water versus under the water.
normal.cn: emerge 与 submerge 是同一个动词配相反前缀：从水里出来，与到水下去。

normal.en: The base mergere means 'to sink'; emerge is what a sunk thing does when it comes back up.
normal.cn: 词基 mergere 意为“沉”；emerge 就是沉下去的东西重新浮上来时做的事。

normal.en: Merge is the same root: things that sink into each other become one.
normal.cn: merge 是同一词根：彼此沉入对方的东西合为一体。

normal.en: Emergency began as 'an unforeseen emergence' — something that suddenly came up.
normal.cn: emergency 最初是“意外冒出的事”——突然升上来的东西。

normal.en: In journalism, it emerged that marks a fact breaking the surface of secrecy.
normal.cn: 在新闻里，it emerged that 标记的是一个事实冲破秘密的水面。

abstract.en: Emergence is what happens when a system produces something none of its parts could contain.
abstract.cn: 涌现，是一个系统生出了它的任何部分都装不下的东西。

abstract.en: Truth does not arrive; it surfaces, and the delay is part of its shape.
abstract.cn: 真相不是被送达的，而是浮上来的；那段延迟本身就是它的形状。

abstract.en: Every leader is a figure the crowd was already standing in.
abstract.cn: 每个领袖，都是人群本来就站在其中的一个身影。

examples.en: The divers waited for the seal to emerge near the far side of the reef.
examples.cn: 潜水员等着那只海豹在礁石远端浮出水面。

examples.en: It emerged during the trial that the signature had been forged.
examples.cn: 审判中曝出，那个签名是伪造的。

examples.en: Several small parties emerged as serious challengers in the election.
examples.cn: 几个小党在选举中崛起为有力的挑战者。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一门儿挤”——潜艇被挤在一门儿窄水道里，只好慢慢浮出水面 → emerge 浮现、出现

root: 源自拉丁语 emergere“升出、冒出”，由 ex“出、向外”+ mergere“浸、沉”构成；词基 mergere 也是 merge（合并）与 submerge（下沉）的来源。核心是“原本沉在下面的东西靠浮力升出表面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of emerge, all one movement: something that was below, behind, or hidden rises above the surface and becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: emerge 的九个义项是同一个动作：原本在下面、在后面或藏起来的东西升到表面之上，变得可见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark water surface; something rises from below and breaks through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色的水面；有东西从下方升起，破水而出。

branches.en: MEDIUM: water and soil are both a dark substance that hides a body until it rises through the top.
branches.cn: 介质：水与土壤都是深色的介质，先把东西藏住，直到它从上面升出来。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: leave the bush, leave the fog — concealment ends and a figure stands in the open.
branches.cn: 可见：离开灌木、离开雾——遮蔽结束，身影站到开阔处。

branches.en: TIME AND TRUTH: a hidden fact and a finished crisis both come up into the open, one into knowledge, one into relief.
branches.cn: 时间与真相：被隐瞒的事实与结束的危机都升到明处，一个进入认知，一个进入解脱。

branches.en: BEING: a new class and a new property arise because conditions at the surface changed.
branches.cn: 存在：新的阶层与新的性质之所以出现，是因为表面的条件变了。

branches.en: RANK: in a crowd everyone is level; the one who rises above the line is seen as the winner.
branches.cn: 位次：人群里人人齐平；升到那条线之上的人，被看作胜者。

intro.en: Emerge's family hangs on Latin mergere 'to sink'. Prefixes decide the direction: ex- up and out, sub- down and under, in- into. Suffixes mark the process, the thing that arises, and the sudden case.
intro.cn: emerge 的词族挂在拉丁语 mergere“沉”上。前缀决定方向：ex- 向上向外，sub- 向下在下，in- 向内。后缀标记过程、升起之物与突发情形。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are mergere 'to dip, sink', emergere 'to rise out', emergens 'rising out', and mersus 'dipped'. They also explain merge and submerge.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 mergere“浸、沉”、emergere“升出”、emergens“升起的”与 mersus“被浸入的”。它们同时也解释了 merge 与 submerge。

items.meaning: the process of coming forth or appearing
items.meaningCN: 出现、显现的过程（-ence 构成过程名词）
items.example: The emergence of online banking changed the branch network.
items.exampleCN: 网络银行的兴起改变了网点布局。

items.meaning: in the process of appearing or newly arisen
items.meaningCN: 正在出现的；新生的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: Emergent technologies rarely arrive with clear rules.
items.exampleCN: 新兴技术到来时很少带着明确规则。

items.meaning: newly appearing and still growing, as in emerging markets
items.meaningCN: 新近出现且仍在成长的，如“新兴市场”（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: Investors moved money into emerging markets.
items.exampleCN: 投资者把资金转向新兴市场。

items.meaning: a sudden situation that demands immediate action
items.meaningCN: 需要立即行动的突发局面（-cy 构成状态名词）
items.example: The plane made an emergency landing.
items.exampleCN: 飞机进行了紧急迫降。

items.meaning: to appear again after being absent or hidden
items.meaningCN: 消失或隐藏之后再次出现（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The old argument re-emerged during the debate.
items.exampleCN: 那场旧争论在辩论中再次浮现。

items.meaning: to put or go under water
items.meaningCN: 使沉入水下；潜入水中（sub- 表示“在下”）
items.example: High tide submerged the lower path.
items.exampleCN: 涨潮淹没了下面的小路。

items.meaning: to sink into one another and become a single thing
items.meaningCN: 彼此沉入对方，合成一体（同一词根的另一支）
items.example: The two firms merged last spring.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司去年春天合并了。

items.meaning: of a plant part, standing above the water surface
items.meaningCN: 指植物器官高出水面的（植物学用语）
items.example: The leaves are emersed above the still water.
items.exampleCN: 叶片挺立在静水之上。

items.meaning: the act of rising out of water; also the reappearance of a star from behind a planet
items.meaningCN: 从水中升出的动作；也指恒星由行星后重新出现（天文）
items.example: Astronomers timed the emersion of the star.
items.exampleCN: 天文学家记录了那颗星的复现时刻。

items.meaning: to come out of a place, period, or condition
items.meaningCN: 从某处、某时期或某状态中出来（from 标记起点）
items.example: The industry emerged from the recession smaller but leaner.
items.exampleCN: 该行业走出衰退时规模更小，却更精干。

latinEntries.meaning: to rise out or up, come forth

latinEntries.meaningCN: 正在升出的；正在冒出的

definition_zh: 强调；着重；突出；重读；使显著
definition_en: to give special force or importance to a word, an idea, or a feature so that others notice it
core_image: 一束光打到舞台中央：别的都退到暗处，被照的那一处格外亮。
scene: She emphasized the word never, and the whole room went quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 emphasize 是「重读某个词、加重语气」（第 1 个义项：语音重读）；句意：她把 never 这个词读得很重，整个房间安静下来。场景要点：加重的手势、被重读的那个词、突然的安静。

pos.zh: 强调；着重；突出；使显著

derivatives.zh: 强调的；断然的；语气强烈的

senses.title: Put stress on a spoken word
senses.titleCN: 语音重读：把某个词念得更重
senses.definition: to say a word or syllable with more force so that it stands out in speech
senses.definitionCN: 用更大的力气说出某个词或音节，使它在话语中格外突出
senses.example: He emphasized the word urgent and looked straight at me.
senses.exampleCN: 他把 urgent 这个词读得很重，并直直地看着我。
senses.why: Greek phainein means 'to show'. Extra voice force is the simplest way to make one word show more than its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phainein 意为“显示”。加大嗓音的力度，就是让一个词比周围词“显示”得更多的最简单办法。

senses.title: Give an idea special importance
senses.titleCN: 强调观点：把重要性压上去
senses.definition: to treat an idea or point as specially important in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作中把某个想法或要点当作特别重要
senses.example: The report emphasizes prevention rather than treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告强调的是预防而非治疗。
senses.why: The word is no longer just loud; the speaker is ranking ideas. What is emphasized is lifted above the rest of the argument.
senses.whyCN: 这里不只是读得响，说者还在给观点排位。被强调的，被抬到整段论证之上。

senses.title: Draw attention to a feature
senses.titleCN: 突出特征：让某处被看见
senses.definition: to make a particular quality or detail noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 使某个特点或细节变得显眼
senses.example: The design emphasizes the building's horizontal lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计突出了建筑的横向线条。
senses.why: Showing is now visual: the feature is brought forward while other features recede, as if lit on a stage.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“显示”是视觉性的：该特征被推到前面，其他特征退后，就像舞台上被打光的那一处。

senses.title: Repeat a point to make it clear
senses.titleCN: 反复申明：用重复加重
senses.definition: to say something again, or in stronger words, so that no one misses it
senses.definitionCN: 再说一遍，或用更强的话说，使没人会漏掉
senses.example: Let me emphasize that no one is being dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 我要强调一下，没有人会被辞退。
senses.why: Repetition adds weight. The repeated sentence is like a second spotlight on the same spot, which makes the importance unmistakable.
senses.whyCN: 重复会增加分量。重说一遍的句子，就像在同一处再打一束光，使重要性无可置疑。

senses.title: Design: make a shape stand out
senses.titleCN: 设计突出：用对比让形体跳出
senses.definition: in design, to give a shape, colour, or element more visual weight than the rest
senses.definitionCN: 在设计上给某个形状、颜色或元素比其余部分更强的视觉分量
senses.example: A single red door emphasizes the symmetry of the facade.
senses.exampleCN: 一扇红门突出了立面的对称。
senses.why: The Greek image of 'showing' works by contrast: one element is made to appear while the others are made to serve as ground.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语“显示”的意象靠对比生效：让一个元素显现出来，同时让其他元素充当背景。

senses.title: Art: bring a subject out of the dark
senses.titleCN: 绘画突出：用明暗把主体托出
senses.definition: in painting or photography, to make the main subject more prominent by light, colour, or focus
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画或摄影中，用光线、色彩或焦点使主体更醒目
senses.example: The painter emphasized the face with a warm light from below.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用来自下方的暖光突出了面部。
senses.why: This is the most literal version of 'make visible': light is put where the painter wants the eye to land.
senses.whyCN: 这是“使之可见”最字面的版本：光被放在画家希望目光落下的地方。

senses.title: Insist on a rule or requirement
senses.titleCN: 强调要求：不容打折扣
senses.definition: to state a rule or requirement firmly so that it is treated as non-negotiable
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地说明某条规则或要求，使其被视为不可商量
senses.example: The coach emphasized that lateness would not be tolerated.
senses.exampleCN: 教练强调，迟到不会被容忍。
senses.why: The added force is no longer about clarity but about authority: the requirement is placed where no one can argue it away.
senses.whyCN: 这里加的分量无关清楚，而关乎权威：要求被放到一个没人能辩掉的位置。

senses.title: Typography: mark text as important
senses.titleCN: 排版强调：用斜体、加粗标出
senses.definition: to set a word in italics, bold, or capitals so that the reader notices it
senses.definitionCN: 用斜体、加粗或大写排印某个词，使读者注意到
senses.example: The editor emphasized the warning by setting it in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把警告加粗排印，以作强调。
senses.why: Ink replaces voice: a change of letterform is the printed equivalent of speaking a word louder.
senses.whyCN: 油墨替代了嗓音：字形的变化，就是印刷版的“把词念得更响”。

senses.title: Restate in order to prevent a misunderstanding
senses.titleCN: 着重说明：把易误解处点明
senses.definition: to state something again in a precise way because it might be misunderstood
senses.definitionCN: 因为某处可能被误解，而用更精确的方式重说一遍
senses.example: She emphasized that the deadline applied only to the first draft.
senses.exampleCN: 她着重说明，截止期限只针对初稿。
senses.why: Here emphasis repairs meaning. The speaker shines light on the exact boundary of a statement so no wrong reading survives.
senses.whyCN: 这里的强调是在修补意义。说者把光照在一句话的确切边界上，使错误读法无处存活。

intro.en: Emphasize was formed in English in the 18th century from emphasis, which came through Latin from Greek. Its Greek core is en 'in' + phainein 'to show'.
intro.cn: emphasize 是 18 世纪在英语中由 emphasis 构成的，而 emphasis 经拉丁语来自希腊语。希腊语的核心是 en“在内”+ phainein“显示”。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to show, bring to light, make visible'. It goes back to PIE *bha- 'to shine', the root behind English words about light and appearance.
items.cn: phainein 意为“显示、带到光下、使可见”。它上溯到原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，这是英语中一批关于光与显现的词根。

items.en: Emphasis meant 'an appearing in, outward appearance'. In rhetoric it came to mean 'significance, indirect meaning' — more than the words literally say.
items.cn: emphasis 意为“显现于内、外表”。在修辞学中转而指“意义、言外之意”——比字面所说的更多。

items.en: Latin borrowed emphasis directly from Greek. In Latin, the plain word for this idea was significatio, and emphasis kept the flavour of an extra, suggested force.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 emphasis。拉丁语里表达这个概念的本族词是 significatio，而 emphasis 保留了“额外、暗示性的力量”这一色彩。

items.en: English takes emphasis in the 1570s meaning 'intensity of expression'. It then narrows to vocal stress on a word as a clue that more is meant.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 70 年代借入 emphasis，意为“表达强度”。随后缩小为“对某个词的重读”，作为“言外有意”的线索。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1765, formed from emphasis + -ize. English already had the adjective emphatic from Greek energetikos-like forms; the verb came last.
items.cn: 动词 1765 年见于记录，由 emphasis + -ize 构成。英语先有形容词 emphatic（来自希腊语相关形式），动词出现得最晚。

items.en: The word now covers voice, writing, design, and typography. De-emphasize (1938) and re-emphasize were added as the need to rank emphasis grew.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖语音、写作、设计与排版。随着“给强调分级”的需要增长，又补出了 de-emphasize（1938）与 re-emphasize。

note.en: The first group is the emphasis family plus one word that is repeatedly confused with it; the second collects verbs that also add weight to a point.
note.cn: 第一组是 emphasis 词族，外加一个常被与它混淆的词；第二组收同样给观点加重的动词。

entries.definition: special importance or force given to something; also vocal stress. Emphasize is the verb built on this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某物的特别重要性或力量；也指重音。emphasize 就是在这个名词上构成的动词。

entries.definition: said or done with force; definite and forceful. It describes the result, while emphasize names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 说得或做得有力的；断然的。它描述结果，而 emphasize 指动作本身。

entries.definition: to share someone else's feelings. Its root is Greek pathos 'feeling', not phainein 'show'.
entries.definitionCN: 体会他人的感受。它的词根是希腊语 pathos“感受”，而不是 phainein“显示”。

entries.definition: to give something less importance. De- 'opposite of' + emphasize; recorded from 1938.
entries.definitionCN: 降低某物的重要性。de-“相反”+ emphasize；1938 年见于记录。

entries.definition: to give special force to a word or point. In speech it is nearly interchangeable with emphasize; in writing it is slightly more informal.
entries.definitionCN: 给某个词或要点特别的力量。口语中与 emphasize 几乎可互换；书面语中略不正式。

entries.definition: to make something stand out as important or interesting. It stresses drawing the eye rather than adding verbal force.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物作为重要或有趣之处显出来。它强调吸引目光，而非加大言语力度。

entries.definition: to emphasize a point, as if drawing a line under it. The image is literally typographic.
entries.definitionCN: 强调某一点，如同在它下面划一道线。这个意象本身就是排版式的。

entries.definition: to make a feature more noticeable. It is common for design, clothing, and pronunciation, and is more formal than highlight.
entries.definitionCN: 使某个特征更显眼。常用于设计、衣着与发音，比 highlight 更正式。

entries.definition: to emphasize something, often to make it more attractive or important than it is. It carries a hint of exaggeration.
entries.definitionCN: 强调某物，常为使其比实际更有吸引力或更重要。它带一点夸大的意味。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek en 'in' + phainein 'show', giving emphasis; family words emphatic, emphatically, de-emphasize, re-emphasize, overemphasize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 en“在内”+ phainein“显示”，合成 emphasis；词族为 emphatic、emphatically、de-emphasize、re-emphasize、overemphasize。

normal.en: Phainein means 'show' — the same root as phenomenon and fantasy, both about appearing.
normal.cn: phainein 意为“显示”——与 phenomenon、fantasy 同根，二者都与“显现”有关。

normal.en: Emphasis was a rhetorical term for meaning more than the words say; emphasize is to make that extra meaning audible.
normal.cn: emphasis 本是修辞术语，指“比字面说得更多”；emphasize 就是把那点多出来的意思说得让人听见。

normal.en: The verb arrived last: noun 1570s, adjective earlier, verb 1765.
normal.cn: 动词来得最晚：名词 16 世纪 70 年代，形容词更早，动词 1765 年。

normal.en: Bold text is emphasis in ink; a raised voice is emphasis in air.
normal.cn: 加粗是油墨里的强调；提高的嗓音是空气里的强调。

normal.en: De-emphasize and overemphasize show that emphasis can be dialled up or down.
normal.cn: de-emphasize 与 overemphasize 说明强调是可以调高调低的。

abstract.en: To emphasize is to decide what the listener is allowed to forget.
abstract.cn: 强调，就是决定听者被允许忘记什么。

abstract.en: Every emphasis is a small claim about proportion.
abstract.cn: 每一次强调，都是关于“比例”的一次小小主张。

abstract.en: What a text bolds tells you what it fears you will miss.
abstract.cn: 一个文本加粗的地方，暴露了它怕你漏掉什么。

examples.en: The manual emphasizes safety checks before every launch.
examples.cn: 手册强调每次发射前的安全检查。

examples.en: He emphasized his point by repeating the last three words.
examples.cn: 他重复最后三个词，以强调自己的观点。

examples.en: The exhibition emphasizes the artist's early drawings.
examples.cn: 这场展览着重呈现这位艺术家的早期素描。

dict_mnemonic.text: “暗发紫光”——把重点按到暗处也发紫光，让所有人一眼看见 → emphasize 强调、突出

root: 源自希腊语 emphasis“显现、言外之意”，由 en“在内”+ phainein“显示”构成（phainein 上溯原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”）；英语 16 世纪 70 年代借入名词 emphasis，1765 年才由它加 -ize 造出动词 emphasize。核心是“让某处显现得更多”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of emphasize, all one operation: put more force on one element so that it shows more than everything around it.
sensesIntro.cn: emphasize 的九个义项是同一个操作：给某一个元素加上更多力量，使它比周围一切都“显示”得更多。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight on one spot of a dark stage; the rest recedes into shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗舞台上的一束光打在一点；其余部分退入阴影。

branches.en: VOICE: one spoken syllable is pressed harder so it stands out in the stream of speech.
branches.cn: 嗓音：把一个音节念得更用力，使它在话语流中格外突出。

branches.en: ARGUMENT: rank a point, repeat it, or fence off its exact boundary — all ways of controlling what the listener takes away.
branches.cn: 论证：给要点排位、重复它、或划清它的确切边界——都是控制听者带走什么的手段。

branches.en: SIGHT: design, painting, and photography make a feature visible by contrast, light, and focus.
branches.cn: 视觉：设计、绘画与摄影靠对比、光线与焦点，让某个特征变得可见。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: emphasis on a rule turns volume into obligation.
branches.cn: 权威：对规则的强调，把音量变成了义务。

branches.en: INK: a word is set in bold, italics or capitals so the reader's eye stops on it.
branches.cn: 油墨：用加粗、斜体或大写排印一个词，让读者的目光停在那里。

intro.en: Emphasize's family is Greek at the core and English in its endings. The suffixes mark the noun, the adjective, the adverb, and the act; the prefixes raise or lower the amount of emphasis.
intro.cn: emphasize 的词族核心是希腊语，词尾是英语。后缀分别标记名词、形容词、副词与动作；前缀则调节强调的量。

latinIntro.en: Latin only borrowed the Greek noun: emphasis, and the later adjective emphaticus. The true source forms are Greek, so the Latin list stays short and honest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只借入了希腊名词 emphasis 以及后来的形容词 emphaticus。真正的来源形式是希腊语，因此拉丁词条只列可靠的两条。

items.meaning: to give special force or importance to something
items.meaningCN: 给某物特别的力量或重要性（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: They emphasize teamwork over individual speed.
items.exampleCN: 他们强调团队合作胜过个人速度。

items.meaning: special importance, stress, or force given to something
items.meaningCN: 给予某物的特别重要性、重音或力量
items.example: The course places emphasis on speaking.
items.exampleCN: 这门课程把重点放在口语上。

items.meaning: expressed with force; definite
items.meaningCN: 有力表达的；断然的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: She gave an emphatic no.
items.exampleCN: 她断然拒绝。

items.meaning: in a forceful, definite way
items.meaningCN: 强调地；断然地（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: He emphatically denied the rumour.
items.exampleCN: 他断然否认了这一传言。

items.meaning: to give something more importance than it deserves
items.meaningCN: 过分强调；给予超出应得的重要性（over- 表示“过度”）
items.example: Tests overemphasize recall and neglect reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 考试过分强调记忆，忽视推理。

items.meaning: to reduce the importance given to something
items.meaningCN: 降低对某物的强调（de- 表示“相反”，1938 年始见）
items.example: The new layout de-emphasizes advertising.
items.exampleCN: 新版式降低了广告的显著度。

items.meaning: to emphasize something again, often after it was forgotten
items.meaningCN: 再次强调，常因先前被忽略（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The letter re-emphasized the original deadline.
items.exampleCN: 这封信再次强调了原定截止日期。

items.meaning: a pronoun such as myself used for emphasis rather than as an object
items.meaningCN: 用于强调而非作宾语的代词，如 myself（语法术语）
items.example: In I made it myself, myself is an emphatic pronoun.
items.exampleCN: 在 I made it myself 中，myself 是强调代词。

items.meaning: special importance given to a particular subject
items.meaningCN: 对某一主题给予的特别重视（on 标记对象）
items.example: There is too much emphasis on speed.
items.exampleCN: 对速度的强调太多了。

items.meaning: extra force on a word to signal contrast or emotion
items.meaningCN: 为表示对比或情绪而加在词上的额外力度（语音学术语）
items.example: Emphatic stress moved from the first word to the second.
items.exampleCN: 强调重音从第一个词移到了第二个词。

latinEntries.meaning: rhetorical stress; suggested force beyond the literal words
latinEntries.meaningCN: 修辞重音；字面之外的暗示力量

definition_zh: 经验的；实证的；以观察或实验为依据的
definition_en: based on observation, experiment, or direct experience rather than on theory or pure reasoning
core_image: 一双手在泥地里做记录：结论来自亲手试过、亲眼量过。
scene: The claim sounds plausible, but there is no empirical evidence for it.
sceneCN: 这里 empirical 是「以观察或实验数据为依据的」（第 1 个义项：实证的）；句意：这个说法听起来合理，却没有实证证据。场景要点：数据表、实验记录本、待验证的假设。

pos.zh: 经验的；实证的；以观察或实验为依据的

derivatives.zh: 以经验为依据地；实证地
经验性的；经验派医生；江湖医生

senses.title: Based on observation and experiment
senses.titleCN: 实证的：结论来自观察与实验
senses.definition: based on what can be observed, measured, or tested rather than on theory alone
senses.definitionCN: 以可观察、可测量或可检验的东西为依据，而非仅凭理论
senses.example: The hypothesis has strong empirical support.
senses.exampleCN: 这个假说有强有力的实证支持。
senses.why: Greek empeiria is 'experience', from en 'in' + peira 'trial'. Knowledge that comes from having been in the trial is knowledge from the test, not from reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 empeiria 是“经验”，由 en“在内”+ peira“试炼”构成。来自“身在试炼之中”的知识，就是来自检验的知识，而不是推理的知识。

senses.title: Medical: a physician guided by experience
senses.titleCN: 医学经验派：靠临床经验治病
senses.definition: in the history of medicine, describing a school of physicians who treated by practical experience rather than by theory
senses.definitionCN: 在医学史上，指依靠实际经验而非理论来治病的医生流派
senses.example: The empiric school trusted observed outcomes over ancient texts.
senses.exampleCN: 经验派更相信观察到的结果，而不是古代典籍。
senses.why: The word entered English in the 1560s in medicine, where 'the experienced doctor' was a real professional label, and the source of empirical.
senses.whyCN: 这个词 16 世纪 60 年代正是以医学义进入英语的，“有经验的医生”是一个真实的职业标签，也是 empirical 的来源。

senses.title: Evidence that can be checked
senses.titleCN: 实证证据：能被别人复核
senses.definition: of evidence, able to be checked by others through observation or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 指证据能被他人通过观察或测量来复核
senses.example: The paper offers empirical evidence from three field sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文提供了来自三个田野点的实证证据。
senses.why: A trial is repeatable. Empirical evidence is what another person could have found by running the same observation, so it is public rather than private.
senses.whyCN: 试炼是可重复的。实证证据就是别人做同样的观察也能得到的东西，因此它是公共的，而不是私人的。

senses.title: Testable by observation
senses.titleCN: 可检验：能被现实驳倒
senses.definition: of a claim, stated so that observation or experiment could show it to be false
senses.definitionCN: 指一个说法表述得能被观察或实验证明为假
senses.example: A good theory must make empirically testable predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论必须做出可实证检验的预测。
senses.why: Peira is a trial that can fail. A claim tied to a test is exposed to failure, and that exposure is exactly what makes it empirical.
senses.whyCN: peira 是可能失败的试炼。与检验绑在一起的说法就暴露在失败面前，而这种暴露正是它“实证”的原因。

senses.title: Research done in the field
senses.titleCN: 实证研究：走出去收数据
senses.definition: describing research that collects data from real cases, surveys, or experiments rather than from argument
senses.definitionCN: 指从真实案例、调查或实验中收集数据的研究，而非靠论证
senses.example: Her empirical work involved two years of interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她的实证研究包含两年的访谈。
senses.why: The researcher goes into the trial rather than watching from outside. Empirical marks the difference between data gathering and armchair reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 研究者是走进试炼里的，而不是在外面看着。empirical 标记的正是“收数据”与“坐而论道”的差别。

senses.title: Chemistry: the simplest formula from experiment
senses.titleCN: 化学经验式：由实验测出的最简比
senses.definition: in chemistry, a formula giving the ratio of atoms measured by experiment, not the actual molecular structure
senses.definitionCN: 化学中由实验测得的原子比例式，而非真实分子结构式
senses.example: Glucose has the empirical formula CH2O.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄糖的经验式为 CH2O。
senses.why: The ratio is what experiment gives you; the true molecular count needs further work. So this formula is literally the empirical one.
senses.whyCN: 实验直接给出的是比例；真实的分子原子数还要再做工作。因此这个式子字面上就是“经验得到的式子”。

senses.title: Statistics: probability from observed frequency
senses.titleCN: 统计经验概率：由已发生的频率估计
senses.definition: in statistics, describing probability estimated from how often something has actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中，指根据某事实际发生的频率估计出的概率
senses.example: The empirical probability of rain here in May is about one in three.
senses.exampleCN: 这里五月的经验降雨概率约为三分之一。
senses.why: Instead of a model, you count what happened. The trial has already been run many times, and the number is read off the record.
senses.whyCN: 不靠模型，而是去数已发生的事。试炼已经重复多次，数字是从记录里读出来的。

senses.title: Old use: relying on mere experience
senses.titleCN: 旧义贬用：单凭经验、不懂理论
senses.definition: in older usage, describing someone who relies on experience without proper knowledge, sometimes meaning a quack
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指只凭经验而无正当知识的人，有时含“江湖医生”之意
senses.example: The learned physicians dismissed him as a mere empiric.
senses.exampleCN: 学院派医生只把他当江湖医生看待。
senses.why: Greek empeiria could mean 'mere practice without knowledge'. When theory was the mark of a real doctor, experience alone became an insult.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 empeiria 可指“只有实践而无知识”。当理论被视为真正医生的标志时，单凭经验就成了一种贬低。

senses.title: Philosophy: the factual as opposed to the normative
senses.titleCN: 哲学实然：经验事实对照规范
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing questions about what is the case, as opposed to what ought to be
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指关于“实际如何”的问题，与“应当如何”相对
senses.example: The essay separates empirical questions from normative ones.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把经验性问题与规范性问题分开。
senses.why: What is the case can be observed; what ought to be cannot. Empirical marks the side of that line where observation has authority.
senses.whyCN: “实际如何”可以被观察，“应当如何”不能。empirical 标记的是这条线的这一侧——观察在此有权威。

intro.en: Empirical came into English as a medical word from Greek empeiria 'experience', built on en 'in' and peira 'trial'. The whole family is about knowledge earned by being tested.
intro.cn: empirical 作为医学词进入英语，来自希腊语 empeiria“经验”，由 en“在内”与 peira“试炼”构成。整个词族都关于“经检验而得的知识”。

items.en: Peira meant 'trial, attempt, experiment'. It belongs to PIE *per- (3) 'to try, risk', an extended sense of the root 'forward' — to press forward across something is to risk it.
items.cn: peira 意为“试炼、尝试、实验”。它属于原始印欧语 *per-（第 3 义）“试、冒风险”，这是词根“向前”的引申义——向前越过某物，就是冒它的险。

items.en: Empeiros meant 'experienced in a thing, proven by use', from en 'in' + peira. The person has been inside the trial, not beside it.
items.cn: empeiros 意为“在某事上有经验的、经使用验证的”，由 en“在内”+ peira 构成。这个人是在试炼之中，而不是在旁边。

items.en: Empeiria was 'experience', and in medicine could also mean 'mere practice without knowledge'. That ambiguity later supplies the insulting sense of empiric.
items.cn: empeiria 是“经验”，在医学语境中也可指“只有实践而无知识”。这一含混后来提供了 empiric 的贬义。

items.en: Latin empiricus, borrowed from Greek, meant 'a physician guided by experience'. English took the adjective empirical from this Latin form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 empiricus 借自希腊语，意为“凭经验治病的医生”。英语的形容词 empirical 就是从这个拉丁形式来的。

items.en: Empirical is first recorded in the 1560s in medicine, meaning 'pertaining to or derived from experience or experiments'. The general sense 'guided by mere experience' is from 1757.
items.cn: empirical 最早见于 16 世纪 60 年代的医学语境，意为“与经验或实验有关、由之而来的”。“仅凭经验指导”的一般义始于 1757 年。

items.en: Empirically (1640s, 'by means of observation and experiment') became the adverb of the scientific method. Empirical now contrasts with theoretical and normative.
items.cn: empirically（17 世纪 40 年代，“通过观察与实验”）成了科学方法的副词。empirical 如今与 theoretical、normative 相对。

note.en: The first group is the empiric family plus a common spelling trap; the second collects words about knowledge from evidence.
note.cn: 第一组是 empiric 词族，外加一个常见的拼写陷阱；第二组收“以证据求知”的同类词。

entries.definition: based on experience; also a physician who works by experience, often with a negative tone. It is the older form behind empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 以经验为依据的；也指凭经验治病的医生，常带贬义。它是 empirical 之前更早的形式。

entries.definition: the view that knowledge comes from experience and observation. It is the noun of empirical, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 认为知识来自经验与观察的主张。它是 empirical 的名词派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a group of states ruled by one power. It comes from Latin imperium 'command', with no link to peira 'trial'.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个强权统治的若干国家。它来自拉丁语 imperium“命令”，与 peira“试炼”无关。

entries.definition: relating to an empire or emperor. Like empire, it belongs to imperium, not to empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 与帝国或皇帝有关的。和 empire 一样，它属于 imperium，与 empirical 无关。

entries.definition: based on tests deliberately set up. It names the method; empirical can also cover plain observation without a designed test.
entries.definitionCN: 以刻意设置的检验为依据的。它指方法；empirical 也可涵盖没有设计过的纯观察。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording without intervening. It is narrower than empirical and often contrasts with experimental.
entries.definitionCN: 以不干预的观察与记录为依据的。它比 empirical 窄，常与 experimental 相对。

entries.definition: based on personal experience. It is about what a person has lived through, not about public data.
entries.definitionCN: 以个人经历为依据的。它说的是一个人经历过什么，而不是公共数据。

entries.definition: judging by practical results rather than theory. It shares the anti-theory attitude but not the demand for evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 以实际结果而非理论来判断。它同样反理论，但不要求证据。

entries.definition: holding that real knowledge comes only from observable facts. It is a philosophical position built on the same demand as empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 主张真正的知识只来自可观察事实。它是以与 empirical 相同的诉求建立的一种哲学立场。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek en 'in' + peira 'trial', giving empeiria 'experience'; family words empiric, empiricism, empiricist, empirically, experiential and experiment (same PIE root).
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 en“在内”+ peira“试炼”，合成 empeiria“经验”；词族为 empiric、empiricism、empiricist、empirically，以及同源印欧词根的 experiential、experiment。

normal.en: Peira is a trial; empeiros is someone who has been inside the trial — hence 'experienced'.
normal.cn: peira 是试炼；empeiros 是走进试炼里的人——因此是“有经验的”。

normal.en: Experiment and empirical share the same PIE root *per- 'to try, risk'.
normal.cn: experiment 与 empirical 共享同一个原始印欧词根 *per-“试、冒风险”。

normal.en: Empirical evidence is evidence someone else could have collected the same way.
normal.cn: 实证证据，就是别人用同样方式也能收集到的证据。

normal.en: Empirical formula in chemistry is the ratio experiment actually gives you, not the full structure.
normal.cn: 化学经验式是实验真正给出的比例，而不是完整结构。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with empire: imperium is 'command', peira is 'trial'.
normal.cn: 别和 empire 混：imperium 是“命令”，peira 是“试炼”。

abstract.en: Empirical means letting the world have the last word.
abstract.cn: 实证，就是让世界拥有最后发言权。

abstract.en: A claim that cannot fail is not empirical, however confident it sounds.
abstract.cn: 一个不可能失败的说法，无论听起来多自信，都不是实证的。

abstract.en: Experience is what remains after the trial has taken something from you.
abstract.cn: 经验，是试炼从你身上拿走一些东西之后留下的东西。

examples.en: There is little empirical support for the claim that the policy reduced crime.
examples.cn: 认为该政策降低了犯罪率的说法缺乏实证支持。

examples.en: The team designed an empirical study with a control group.
examples.cn: 团队设计了一项带对照组的实证研究。

examples.en: The empirical formula tells you the ratio, not the number of atoms in a molecule.
examples.cn: 经验式给出的是比例，而不是分子中的原子数。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬皮瑞克”——硬邦邦的皮面记录本里全是实验数据，一页页都是验过的 → empirical 实证的、经验的

root: 源自希腊语 empeiria“经验”，由 en“在内”+ peira“试炼、实验”构成（peira 属原始印欧语 *per-“试、冒风险”，与 experiment、experience 同源）；拉丁语 empiricus 指“凭经验治病的医生”，英语 16 世纪 60 年代以医学义借入形容词 empirical。核心是“经亲历检验而得”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of empirical, all one standard: a claim counts only if observation or experiment can support or refute it.
sensesIntro.cn: empirical 的九个义项都遵循同一条标准：一个说法只有在观察或实验能支持或驳倒它时才算数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notebook of measurements taken by hand, in the field, with results crossed out and repeated.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本在田野里手写的测量记录，结果被划掉又重做。

branches.en: METHOD: observation, public evidence, and field research are three levels of the same demand that knowledge be checked.
branches.cn: 方法：观察、公共证据、田野研究，是“知识必须被检验”这一要求的三个层级。

branches.en: HISTORY: the experienced physician was once a professional label, and later, when theory ruled, the same word became an insult.
branches.cn: 历史：经验派医生曾是职业标签；后来理论当道，同一个词又成了贬称。

branches.en: FORMAL USES: the empirical formula of chemistry and the empirical probability of statistics both turn observation into a figure.
branches.cn: 形式用法：化学的经验式与统计的经验概率，都把观察变成一个数字。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: the line between what is and what ought to be is drawn by whether observation can settle it.
branches.cn: 哲学：“实际如何”与“应当如何”之间的线，由“观察能否裁定”来划。

branches.en: RISK: peira is a trial that can fail; being empirical means stating things so that the world may say no.
branches.cn: 风险：peira 是可能失败的试炼；做实证，就是把话说得能被世界回答“不”。

intro.en: Empirical's family is Greek at the root and Latin in its endings. Suffixes mark the method, the doctrine, the person, and the adverb; the prefixes deny or oppose the empirical stance.
intro.cn: empirical 的词族根部是希腊语，词尾是拉丁语。后缀标记方法、学说、人与副词；前缀则否定或反对实证立场。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin form is empiricus 'physician guided by experience', borrowed from Greek. The Greek chain empeiria, empeiros, peira is the real source and is listed separately in the items.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是借自希腊语的 empiricus“凭经验治病的医生”。真正的来源是希腊语链 empeiria、empeiros、peira，已在词条中单列说明。

items.meaning: based on observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 以观察或实验为依据的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The conclusion rests on empirical data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结论建立在实测数据上。

items.meaning: by means of observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 通过观察或实验地（-ly 构成副词，17 世纪 40 年代始见）
items.example: The question can be settled empirically.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题可以用实证方式解决。

items.meaning: the doctrine that knowledge comes from experience
items.meaningCN: 认为知识来自经验的学说（-ism 构成主义名词）
items.example: British empiricism shaped modern psychology.
items.exampleCN: 英国经验主义塑造了现代心理学。

items.meaning: a supporter of empiricism
items.meaningCN: 经验主义者（-ist 构成人名词）
items.example: As an empiricist, she distrusts pure deduction.
items.exampleCN: 作为经验主义者，她不信任纯演绎。

items.meaning: based on experience; an experience-based physician
items.meaningCN: 凭经验的；经验派医生（比 empirical 更早的形式）
items.example: The empiric tradition favoured bedside observation.
items.exampleCN: 经验派传统偏重床旁观察。

items.meaning: not based on observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 不以观察或实验为依据的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: The theory makes several non-empirical assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 这个理论有几条非经验的假设。

items.meaning: opposed to treating observation as the final test
items.meaningCN: 反对把观察当作最终检验的（anti- 表示“反对”）
items.example: His anti-empirical stance made the review controversial.
items.exampleCN: 他的反实证立场使这篇评论引起争议。

items.meaning: used in compounds meaning 'empirical and ...', as in empirico-critical
items.meaningCN: 构词成分，表示“经验的与……的”，如 empirico-critical（经验批判的）
items.example: The school is known for its empirico-critical method.
items.exampleCN: 这一学派以经验批判方法著称。

items.meaning: evidence obtained by observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 通过观察或实验获得的证据
items.example: The court asked for empirical evidence, not opinion.
items.exampleCN: 法庭要的是实证证据，不是意见。

items.meaning: a formula giving the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
items.meaningCN: 给出原子最简整数比的化学式（化学术语）
items.example: The empirical formula is CH2O; the molecular formula is C6H12O6.
items.exampleCN: 经验式是 CH2O，分子式是 C6H12O6。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 有经验的；经使用验证的

latinEntries.structure: Greek noun, from PIE *per- 'to try, risk'

definition_zh: 使能够；使可能；启用；授权；使具备条件
definition_en: to give someone or something the means, ability, or conditions to do something, or to make a function possible
core_image: 把工具放进对方手里：手原来空着，现在握得住、做得成。
scene: The scholarship enabled her to study abroad for a year.
sceneCN: 这里 enable 是「使某人有能力、有条件做某事」（第 1 个义项：给予能力/条件）；句意：这笔奖学金使她得以在国外学习一年。场景要点：录取信、机票、账本上凑齐的数字。

pos.zh: 使能够；使成为可能；启用；授权

collocations.zh: 使残障人士获得能力／便利

derivatives.zh: 使能者；赋能者；（心理）纵容者
使失去能力；停用；使残障

senses.title: Give someone the means to do something
senses.titleCN: 使人有能力：把条件交到手里
senses.definition: to give a person the ability, opportunity, or resources needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做成某事所需的能力、机会或资源
senses.example: The grant enabled the lab to buy its first electron microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助使实验室买得起第一台电子显微镜。
senses.why: Able comes from Latin habilis 'easily handled', from habere 'to hold'. To enable is to put something into someone's hands that they can now hold and use.
senses.whyCN: able 来自拉丁语 habilis“容易握住的”，源头是 habere“握有”。enable 就是把某样东西放进对方手里，让他现在握得住、用得上。

senses.title: Make an outcome possible
senses.titleCN: 使成为可能：把门打开
senses.definition: to make something possible that was not possible before
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不可能的事成为可能
senses.example: Cheap sensors enabled a new kind of weather network.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价传感器使一种新型气象网络成为可能。
senses.why: The held object is now a condition rather than a tool. Once the condition is in place, the outcome can follow, so enabling becomes making possible.
senses.whyCN: 被握住的从工具变成了条件。条件一到位，结果就能跟上，于是“使能”变成“使可能”。

senses.title: Technology: make a capability work
senses.titleCN: 技术使能：让某项能力运转
senses.definition: of a technology or system, to make a capability available or workable
senses.definitionCN: 指某项技术或系统使某种能力可用或可运转
senses.example: The chip enables real-time translation on a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚芯片使手机上的实时翻译成为可能。
senses.why: A component holds the power for the whole device. The part 'gives the hand' to the system, which is why engineers speak of enabling technologies.
senses.whyCN: 一个部件握有为整台设备供能的本事。这个部件把“手”给了系统，所以工程师会说 enabling technologies（使能技术）。

senses.title: Computing: switch a feature on
senses.titleCN: 设置启用：把开关打开
senses.definition: in software or settings, to turn on an option so that it becomes active
senses.definitionCN: 在软件或设置中打开某个选项，使其生效
senses.example: Enable two-factor authentication in the security settings.
senses.exampleCN: 在安全设置里启用双重验证。
senses.why: Here the means already exists; the user only releases it. The verb marks the moment the capability is allowed to operate.
senses.whyCN: 这里能力已经存在，用户只是把它放出来。动词标记的是“允许该能力开始运转”的那一刻。

senses.title: Law: give legal power to act
senses.titleCN: 法律授权：给予行事的权力
senses.definition: in law, to give a person or body the authority to do something
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上授予某人或某机构做某事的权力
senses.example: The enabling act allowed the agency to set emission limits.
senses.exampleCN: 授权法允许该机构设定排放上限。
senses.why: An enabling act hands legal capacity to a body. The metaphor is exact: authority is the thing placed in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 授权法把法律上的能力交到某机构手里。这个比喻很准确：权力就是被放进手中的那件东西。

senses.title: Provide the resources for something
senses.titleCN: 提供资源：给出本钱
senses.definition: to supply money, time, or equipment that makes an activity feasible
senses.definitionCN: 提供使某项活动可行的资金、时间或设备
senses.example: Remote work was enabled by cheap bandwidth and cloud storage.
senses.exampleCN: 远程办公靠廉价带宽与云存储才得以实现。
senses.why: Resources are the concrete things held. When the supply is enough, the activity can be undertaken; the hand is no longer empty.
senses.whyCN: 资源就是手里握着的具体东西。供给足够，活动才拿得起来；手不再空着。

senses.title: Allow something to happen
senses.titleCN: 促成发生：不去拦它
senses.definition: to make conditions favourable for an event, often without causing it directly
senses.definitionCN: 为某事件创造有利条件，通常并非直接造成它
senses.example: Clear rules enable fair competition rather than preventing it.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的规则促成公平竞争，而不是阻止它。
senses.why: Enabling is not forcing. You put the means in place and then let the event use it, so the verb sits between allowing and causing.
senses.whyCN: 使能不是强迫。你把条件放好，然后让事件去用它，所以这个动词介于“允许”与“造成”之间。

senses.title: Help someone live independently
senses.titleCN: 辅助自立：补上缺的那只手
senses.definition: of equipment, support, or design, to help a person with a disability do things for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 指设备、支持或设计帮助残障人士自己做事情
senses.example: The ramp enables wheelchair users to enter the building unaided.
senses.exampleCN: 坡道使轮椅使用者无需他人帮助就能进入大楼。
senses.why: The missing capacity is supplied by a tool, so the person holds again what the body could not. Enabling here is close to restoring a hand.
senses.whyCN: 缺失的能力由工具补上，人重新握住了身体握不住的东西。这里的 enable 接近于“给别人补一只手”。

senses.title: Psychology: make bad behaviour easier
senses.titleCN: 纵容：让坏行为更容易发生
senses.definition: to make it easier for someone to continue harmful behaviour, often by shielding them from consequences
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更容易继续有害行为，常通过替他挡掉后果
senses.example: By paying his debts, she was enabling his gambling.
senses.exampleCN: 她替他还债，实际上是在纵容他赌博。
senses.why: The same structure of giving means, applied to a harmful habit: what is put into the hand is the ability to keep going. The word turns negative here.
senses.whyCN: 同样是“给条件”的结构，用在了有害习惯上：放进手里的，是“继续下去的能力”。这个词在这里转成了负面。

intro.en: Enable is a native English formation: the prefix en- 'make, put in' added to able, which came from Latin habilis 'easily handled' and habere 'to hold'. Its history is the history of a hand.
intro.cn: enable 是英语本土构成的词：前缀 en-“使、放入”加在 able 上，而 able 来自拉丁语 habilis“容易握住的”与 habere“握有”。它的历史就是一只手的历史。

items.en: Habere meant 'to hold, have, keep'. It is reconstructed from PIE *ghabh- 'to give or receive', so holding and handing over share a root.
items.cn: habere 意为“握有、持有、保有”。它上溯到原始印欧语 *ghabh-“给予或接受”，因此“握有”与“交出”共享一个词根。

items.en: Habilis meant 'easily handled, apt, fit', a verbal adjective from habere. 'Easy to be held' becomes 'fit for a purpose'.
items.cn: habilis 意为“容易握住的、合用的、合适的”，是 habere 的动词性形容词。“容易握住”由此变成“适合某个用途”。

items.en: Old French (h)able 'capable; fitting; agile' carried the Latin sense into English. English dropped the silent h-, though some related words kept it.
items.cn: 古法语 (h)able“有能力的、合适的、灵巧的”把拉丁义带进英语。英语去掉了不发音的 h-，但一些同族词保留了它。

items.en: Enable is recorded in the early 15th century meaning 'to make fit', and by the mid-15th century 'to make able to'. It is en- (1) 'make, put in' + able.
items.cn: enable 于 15 世纪早期见于记录，意为“使合适”，到 15 世纪中期为“使能够”。它由 en-（第 1 义）“使、放入”+ able 构成。

items.en: The legal phrase enabling act is recorded from 1684: an act that empowers a body or person to take certain action.
items.cn: 法律短语 enabling act 于 1684 年见于记录：授予某机构或个人采取某些行动的权力。

items.en: Engineering and computing gave the word new weight: enabling technologies, enable a feature, enable and disable. The old 'put it in the hand' image now covers switches as well as tools.
items.cn: 工程与计算机给这个词添了新分量：enabling technologies、enable a feature、enable and disable。旧的“放进手里”意象，如今既覆盖工具，也覆盖开关。

note.en: The first group is the able family, including its negative twin; the second collects verbs of making something possible.
note.cn: 第一组是 able 词族，含它的否定孪生词；第二组收“使可能”类动词。

entries.definition: having the power or means to do something. Enable is en- 'make' plus this adjective; the adjective is the older word.
entries.definitionCN: 有能力或有办法做某事。enable 是 en-“使”加这个形容词；形容词更早。

entries.definition: to take away the ability to act, or to turn a function off. Dis- 'not, apart' + able is the exact mirror of enable.
entries.definitionCN: 夺去行动能力，或关闭某项功能。dis-“不、分开”+ able 正是 enable 的镜像。

entries.definition: one who or that which enables someone else. In psychology it names a person who shields someone from the consequences of bad behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 使他人获得能力的人或物。在心理学中指替他人挡住坏行为后果的纵容者。

entries.definition: the power or skill to do something. It comes from Latin habilitas, the noun of habilis, not from the verb enable.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的能力或技能。它来自拉丁语 habilitas（habilis 的名词），而非动词 enable。

entries.definition: to let something happen without forbidding it. Allow removes a barrier; enable supplies a means.
entries.definitionCN: 不去禁止，让某事发生。allow 是移开障碍；enable 是提供手段。

entries.definition: to give official permission. It is more formal than allow and says nothing about providing the means.
entries.definitionCN: 正式允许。它比 allow 正式，也不涉及提供手段。

entries.definition: to give someone power or confidence. It is enable applied to authority and self-belief, usually of people rather than systems.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人权力或信心。它是 enable 用在权力与自信上，多用于人而非系统。

entries.definition: to make a process easier. It lowers friction, while enable may supply something that was entirely absent.
entries.definitionCN: 使过程更容易。它降低阻力，而 enable 可能提供的是原本完全缺失的东西。

entries.definition: to supply someone with the tools or skills needed. It is the most concrete version of enable: actual equipment in actual hands.
entries.definitionCN: 为某人提供所需的工具或技能。它是最具体的 enable：真实的装备放进真实的手里。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: en- 'make, put in' + able, from Latin habilis 'easy to hold' and habere 'to hold'; family words disabled, disability, ability, enabler, enablement.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：en-“使、放入”+ able，源头是拉丁语 habilis“容易握住”与 habere“握有”；词族为 disabled、disability、ability、enabler、enablement。

normal.en: Able means 'easy to hold'; enable means putting something holdable into someone's hands.
normal.cn: able 意为“容易握住”；enable 就是把握得住的东西放进别人手里。

normal.en: Disable is the mirror: take the thing back out of the hand.
normal.cn: disable 是镜像：把那件东西从手里拿回去。

normal.en: Ability and able share Latin habilis; the h- that English dropped still shows in words like habilitate.
normal.cn: ability 与 able 共享拉丁语 habilis；英语丢掉的 h- 在 habilitate 一类词里还看得见。

normal.en: In software, enable and disable are literally the same hand opening or closing.
normal.cn: 在软件里，enable 与 disable 就是同一只手在张开或合上。

normal.en: An enabling act hands legal power to a body — authority treated as an object in the hand.
normal.cn: enabling act 把法律权力交到某机构手里——权力被当作手中之物。

abstract.en: To enable is to decide what another person will be able to attempt.
abstract.cn: 使能，就是决定另一个人将有能力去尝试什么。

abstract.en: Every tool quietly rewrites the list of things a person can do.
abstract.cn: 每件工具，都在悄悄改写一个人“能做什么”的清单。

abstract.en: Enabling someone's worst habit is still enabling; the hand does not care what it holds.
abstract.cn: 纵容一个人最坏的习性也仍是“使能”；那只手并不在乎自己握着什么。

examples.en: The new bridge enabled villagers to reach the clinic in twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 新桥使村民二十分钟就能到达诊所。

examples.en: You must enable cookies for the checkout page to work.
examples.cn: 必须启用 Cookie，结算页面才能正常工作。

examples.en: The law enables local councils to set their own housing targets.
examples.cn: 这项法律授权地方议会自行设定住房目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一捏脖”——一捏脖子把人提起来，他就能翻过这道墙 → enable 使能够、使有可能

root: 由英语本土前缀 en-“使、放入”+ able 构成；able 来自古法语 (h)able，再上溯拉丁语 habilis“容易握住的”，词根 habere“握有”（原始印欧语 *ghabh-“给予或接受”）。字面是“把可握住的东西放进手里”，故为“使能够、使可能”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of enable, all one act: something is placed in someone's hand, and a capability that was missing now exists.
sensesIntro.cn: enable 的九个义项是同一个动作：把某样东西放进某人手里，原本缺失的能力于是存在了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty hand; a tool is placed into it, and the fingers close around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只空手；一件工具被放进掌心，手指合拢握住。

branches.en: MEANS: a grant, a sensor, or a supply line all put a condition into the hand, and the act follows.
branches.cn: 手段：资助、传感器、供给线，都是把条件放进手里，行动随后发生。

branches.en: MACHINES: a chip gives a phone its capability; a switch lets an existing capability run.
branches.cn: 机器：芯片把能力给了手机；开关让已有的能力开始运转。

branches.en: LAW: authority is treated as a thing handed over, which is why an enabling act can create power.
branches.cn: 法律：权力被当作被交出的东西，所以授权法能够创造权力。

branches.en: CONDITIONS: favourable rules and accessible design both remove what blocked the act without performing it.
branches.cn: 条件：有利的规则与无障碍设计，都是移除阻碍，而不代替人去行动。

branches.en: DARK SIDE: the same hand can hold the means to continue a harmful habit.
branches.cn: 暗面：同一只手，也可以握有“让坏习惯继续下去”的手段。

intro.en: Enable's family is built on able and its Latin base habilis. The suffixes mark state, person, and process; dis- turns the whole word inside out.
intro.cn: enable 的词族建立在 able 及其拉丁词基 habilis 上。后缀标记状态、人与过程；dis- 则把整个词翻转过来。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are habere 'to hold', habilis 'easy to hold, apt', and habilitas 'ability'. They explain able, ability, and the h- that survives in habilitate.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 habere“握有”、habilis“易握的、合用的”与 habilitas“能力”。它们解释了 able、ability，以及 habilitate 中保留下来的 h-。

items.meaning: to give the means or ability to do something
items.meaningCN: 给予做某事的手段或能力（en- 表示“使、放入”）
items.example: Good lighting enables people to work safely.
items.exampleCN: 良好的照明使人能安全工作。

items.meaning: having been given the means; switched on
items.meaningCN: 已获得手段的；已启用的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: The enabled account can post to the group.
items.exampleCN: 已启用的账号可以在这个群里发帖。

items.meaning: that makes something possible, as in enabling technology
items.meaningCN: 使某事成为可能的，如“使能技术”（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: The internet is an enabling infrastructure.
items.exampleCN: 互联网是一种使能型基础设施。

items.meaning: one who or that which enables; also a person who covers for bad behaviour
items.meaningCN: 使能者；赋能因素；也指纵容他人坏行为的人（-r 构成施事名词）
items.example: A quiet enabler can keep a problem alive for years.
items.exampleCN: 一个沉默的纵容者能让一个问题拖很多年。

items.meaning: the act or process of giving people the means to act
items.meaningCN: 赋予人们行动手段的行为或过程（-ment 构成过程名词）
items.example: Sales enablement trains staff to use the new tools.
items.exampleCN: 销售赋能培训员工使用新工具。

items.meaning: to remove the ability to act, or to switch a function off
items.meaningCN: 夺去行动能力；关闭功能（dis- 表示否定或分离）
items.example: The injury disabled him for six months.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤使他六个月无法行动。

items.meaning: having a condition that limits activity; also switched off
items.meaningCN: 有活动受限状况的；被停用的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The building has parking for disabled visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这栋楼为残障访客设有停车位。

items.meaning: a condition that limits a person's activity
items.meaningCN: 限制个人活动的状况（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The law protects workers with a disability.
items.exampleCN: 法律保护有残障的劳动者。

items.structure: Latin habilis 'easy to hold' via Old French (h)able
items.meaning: having the power or means to do something
items.meaningCN: 有能力或有办法做某事（enable 的词基）
items.example: She was able to finish the race.
items.exampleCN: 她跑完了全程。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something
items.meaningCN: 做事的能力或技能（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The job tests your ability to stay calm.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作要求你具备保持冷静的能力。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb, from PIE *ghabh- 'give or receive'

latinEntries.meaningCN: 容易握住的；合用的；合适的

definition_zh: 遭遇；遇到；偶遇；面临；交锋；会面
definition_en: to meet someone or something, especially unexpectedly or as an opponent, or to experience a difficulty
core_image: 两个人迎面撞上：对方就在正前方，脸对着脸。
