scene: We encountered heavy snow on the pass and had to turn back.
sceneCN: 这里 encounter 是「途中遇到（困难或状况）」（第 3 个义项：遭遇困难）；句意：我们在山口遇到大雪，只好折返。场景要点：山口、被雪埋住的路、掉头的车。

pos.zh: 遭遇；遇到；偶遇；面临
相遇；遭遇；交锋；会面

collocations.zh: 近距离接触（常指与不明飞行物）

derivatives.zh: 反击；对抗；柜台（由 encounter 缩略而来）
可能遇到的；可遭遇的（较少用）
所遇到的；经历过的（多作分词）

senses.title: Meet someone by chance
senses.titleCN: 偶遇某人：不期而遇
senses.definition: to meet a person unexpectedly, without planning to
senses.definitionCN: 事先没有安排地遇到某人
senses.example: I encountered an old teacher on the train to Brighton.
senses.exampleCN: 去布莱顿的火车上，我偶遇了一位老教师。
senses.why: The Latin phrase was in + contra, 'in front of, facing'. Two paths crossing without warning put two faces opposite each other; the oldest sense was hostile, the casual one came later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语是 in + contra，“在……之前、迎面”。两条路线毫无预告地交叉，两张脸就对面了；最早的意思是敌对，随意的“偶遇”是后来才有的。

senses.title: Meet an enemy in battle
senses.titleCN: 迎战：与敌人正面相对
senses.definition: to meet an opponent in combat or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在战斗或冲突中与对手相对
senses.example: The patrol encountered a larger force near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻队在河边遭遇了一支更大的部队。
senses.why: This is the original sense recorded around 1300: to meet as an adversary. Contra is 'against', so the meeting is face to face and hostile.
senses.whyCN: 这是约 1300 年记录的原义：作为对手相遇。contra 意为“对着”，所以这种相遇是面对面且敌对的。

senses.title: Run into a difficulty
senses.titleCN: 遭遇困难：路上撞见阻碍
senses.definition: to experience a problem, danger, or obstacle, often while doing something else
senses.definitionCN: 在做别的事的过程中遇到问题、危险或阻碍
senses.example: The project encountered legal obstacles in its second year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在第二年遭遇了法律障碍。
senses.why: The opponent is no longer a person but a difficulty standing in the path. It still faces you and blocks you, so the hostile image survives.
senses.whyCN: 对手不再是个人，而是立在路上的困难。它仍然正面朝着你、挡住你，所以那份敌对的意象留了下来。

senses.title: Come across a thing or a word
senses.titleCN: 遇到某物：在材料里碰见
senses.definition: to find or see something, especially while looking for something else
senses.definitionCN: 在找别的东西时发现或看到某物
senses.example: Readers will encounter unfamiliar terms in the first chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 读者会在第一章遇到不熟悉的术语。
senses.why: The thing stands in front of you on your way through the text. Meeting becomes finding, with no hostility and no person.
senses.whyCN: 那东西立在你经过文本的路上。相遇由此变成“碰见”，既没有敌意，也没有人。

senses.title: Noun: a short meeting
senses.titleCN: 名词：一次短暂的会面
senses.definition: a meeting with someone, especially one that is brief or not planned
senses.definitionCN: 与某人的会面，尤指短暂或未预先安排的
senses.example: It was a brief encounter at a conference, nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是会议上一次简短的碰面，仅此而已。
senses.why: The noun came first in English, around 1300, meaning a meeting of adversaries. The count noun keeps the event as a single face-to-face moment.
senses.whyCN: 名词在英语中出现更早，约 1300 年，意为“对手的会面”。这个可数名词把事件保留为一个面对面的瞬间。

senses.title: Noun: a clash or confrontation
senses.titleCN: 名词：冲突、交锋
senses.definition: a fight, clash, or serious disagreement between opposing sides
senses.definitionCN: 对立双方之间的打斗、冲突或严重分歧
senses.example: A violent encounter between police and protesters left ten injured.
senses.exampleCN: 警方与抗议者的暴力冲突造成十人受伤。
senses.why: This sense holds the original hostility most openly. The meeting is not neutral contact; it is contact between forces that push against each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项最直白地保留了原初的敌意。会面不是中性的接触，而是两股相互推挤的力量之间的接触。

senses.title: Psychology: an encounter group
senses.titleCN: 心理学：交心团体
senses.definition: in psychology, a group session in which people meet openly to express feelings and learn about themselves
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中的团体活动，参与者坦诚相会、表达感受并认识自我
senses.example: The clinic ran weekend encounter groups for couples.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所周末为伴侣举办交心团体活动。
senses.why: The word is used by Carl Rogers from 1967. Here facing each other is the therapy: the direct encounter is what makes change possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由卡尔·罗杰斯于 1967 年这样使用。在这里，面对面本身就是治疗：直接相遇才使改变成为可能。

senses.title: Biology: meet a species in the field
senses.titleCN: 生物调查：在野外遇见某物种
senses.definition: of a species or specimen, to be found or observed in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 指某物种或标本在某地被发现或观察到
senses.example: Divers encountered several species rarely seen below thirty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员遇到了几种在三十米以下罕见出现的物种。
senses.why: The observer and the organism come face to face in the field. It is the same meeting, recorded as data rather than as a story.
senses.whyCN: 观察者与生物在野外面对面。还是同一次相遇，只是被记成数据而非故事。

senses.title: Formal: face a situation directly
senses.titleCN: 正式：直面某种局面
senses.definition: to have to deal with a situation or person directly and seriously
senses.definitionCN: 必须直接而严肃地应对某种局面或某个人
senses.example: The committee will encounter strong opposition in the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会将在参议院遭遇强烈反对。
senses.why: The verb keeps its Latin facing: to encounter a situation is to stand in front of it rather than avoid it. The confrontation is now procedural.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语的“迎面”：encounter 一种局面，就是站到它面前而不是避开。这种交锋如今是程序性的。

intro.en: Encounter is built on Latin contra 'against'. The French form gave English both a noun and a verb around 1300, first for meeting an enemy, later for any meeting.
intro.cn: encounter 建立在拉丁语 contra“对着”之上。法语形式在约 1300 年为英语同时提供了名词与动词，最早指迎敌，后来指任何相遇。

items.en: Contra meant 'against, opposite, facing'. It comes from *com-teros, with com 'with' and a comparative suffix, originally 'in comparison with'.
items.cn: contra 意为“对着、相反、迎面”，来自 *com-teros，由 com“与”加比较级后缀构成，原义是“与……相比”。

items.en: Incontra meant 'in front of'. In- 'in' + contra 'against' puts one thing directly before another, which is the physical basis of meeting.
items.cn: incontra 意为“在……前面”。in-“在内”+ contra“对着”，把一物放到另一物正前方，这就是“相遇”的物理基础。

items.en: Old French encontre (12c.) meant 'meeting; fight; opportunity', used as both noun and preposition. The verb encontrer meant 'meet, come across; confront, fight'.
items.cn: 古法语 encontre（12 世纪）意为“相遇；战斗；机会”，兼作名词与介词。动词 encontrer 意为“遇见、碰上；对抗、作战”。

items.en: English records both the noun and the verb around 1300. The first sense is hostile: 'meeting of adversaries, confrontation' and 'to meet as an adversary'.
items.cn: 英语在 1300 年前后同时记录了名词与动词。最早的意思是敌对的：“对手的会面、对抗”与“作为对手相遇”。

items.en: The weakened sense 'meet casually or unexpectedly' is recorded by the early 16th century. The hostility drains out, leaving only the fact of two paths crossing.
items.cn: 弱化义“随意或意外相遇”在 16 世纪早期见于记录。敌意流失，只剩两条路线交叉这一事实。

items.en: Carl Rogers gives encounter its therapeutic sense; encounter group is attested from 1967. The old face-to-face image is now used for personal growth.
items.cn: 卡尔·罗杰斯赋予 encounter 治疗义；encounter group 于 1967 年见于记录。旧的面对面意象，如今用于个人成长。

note.en: The first group shares the contra 'against' root or is built from encounter; the second collects verbs of meeting, from neutral to hostile.
note.cn: 第一组共享 contra“对着”词根，或由 encounter 构成；第二组收“相遇”类动词，从中性到敌对。

entries.definition: to oppose or respond to something. It is a shortening of Middle English acountren, encountren.
entries.definitionCN: 反对或回应某事。它是中古英语 acountren、encountren 的缩略。

entries.definition: against; opposite. It is the Latin word that supplies the second half of encounter.
entries.definitionCN: 反对；相反。它就是提供 encounter 后半部的那个拉丁词。

entries.definition: to set two things against each other to show their difference. Contra 'against' + stare 'stand'.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物并置对照以显出差异。contra“对着”+ stare“站”。

entries.definition: a therapy group that meets to express feelings openly. Recorded from 1967 through Carl Rogers.
entries.definitionCN: 以坦诚表达感受为目的的治疗团体。经卡尔·罗杰斯于 1967 年见于记录。

entries.definition: to come together with someone, by plan or not. It is the plain word; encounter usually adds surprise or difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人相聚，可预先安排也可偶然。它最朴素；encounter 通常多了意外或困难。

entries.definition: to face someone or something directly, often with courage or hostility. It stresses the facing, not the fact of meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 直接面对某人或某事，常含勇气或敌意。它强调“面对”，而非相遇这一事实。

entries.definition: to find or meet something by chance. It is used more for objects and texts than for people.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然发现或碰到。它多用于物件与文本，少用于人。

entries.definition: to meet someone unexpectedly, or to hit a problem. It is the spoken equivalent of encounter, informal and often accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 意外遇到某人，或撞上问题。它是 encounter 的口语对应，不正式且多为偶然。

entries.definition: to accept and deal with a difficult situation. It implies willingness; encounter only records that the situation happened.
entries.definitionCN: 接受并应对困难局面。它含“愿意”；encounter 只记录局面发生了。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin in 'in' + contra 'against', giving the French phrase found in encounter; family words counter, contrast, contra, encounter group.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 in“在内”+ contra“对着”，构成 encounter 所由来之法语短语；词族为 counter、contrast、contra、encounter group。

normal.en: Contra is 'against': an encounter is two things ending up face to face.
normal.cn: contra 是“对着”：一次 encounter 就是两样东西最终面对面。

normal.en: Counter is just a worn-down encounter: to counter is to meet a blow with a blow.
normal.cn: counter 就是磨短了的 encounter：反击就是用一击去迎另一击。

normal.en: The first recorded sense is military; the friendly 'bump into' sense arrives 200 years later.
normal.cn: 最早记录的意思是军事性的；友好的“碰见”义晚了两百年才到。

normal.en: Encounter a problem and you are standing in front of it, not beside it.
normal.cn: encounter 一个问题，你就是站在它面前，而不是在旁边。

normal.en: Contrast is the same contra with stare 'stand': two things stood against each other.
normal.cn: contrast 是同一个 contra 加 stare“站”：两样东西对着站。

abstract.en: An encounter is a moment when two futures briefly share the same point.
abstract.cn: 一次相遇，是两个未来短暂地共用了同一个点。

abstract.en: What you meet is often what you were already walking toward.
abstract.cn: 你遇到的东西，常常正是你原本就在走向的东西。

abstract.en: Hostility and intimacy both begin with two faces in front of each other.
abstract.cn: 敌意与亲密，都从两张脸彼此相对开始。

examples.en: They encountered each other again at the same small airport years later.
examples.cn: 多年后，他们在同一座小机场再次相遇。

examples.en: The expedition encountered storms, broken equipment, and a shortage of fuel.
examples.cn: 探险队遭遇了风暴、设备损坏和燃料短缺。

examples.en: Her first encounter with the poem was in a school anthology.
examples.cn: 她第一次接触这首诗，是在一本学校选本里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬扛特”——迎面撞上也只能硬扛，特硬地顶住 → encounter 遭遇、相遇

root: 源自拉丁语 in + contra“对着、迎面”，晚期拉丁语 incontra 意为“在……前面”；经古法语 encontre / encontrer 于约 1300 年进入英语，最初指“与敌人相遇、交锋”，16 世纪早期才弱化为“偶遇”。contra 也是 counter、contrast 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of encounter, all one geometry: two things arrive at the same point and end up facing each other.
sensesIntro.cn: encounter 的九个义项是同一个几何关系：两样东西到达同一点，最终彼此相对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths crossing at a single point, with the two travellers stopped face to face.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路线在一个点上交叉，两个行人停住，面对面。

branches.en: CHANCE: two unrelated plans cross, and the crossing itself becomes a small event, countable as one encounter.
branches.cn: 偶然：两个无关的计划交叉，交叉本身就成了一件小事，可数作一次 encounter。

branches.en: CONFLICT: the original sense, where the face in front of you is an enemy and the meeting is a clash.
branches.cn: 冲突：原初义，正前方那张脸是敌人，相遇就是交锋。

branches.en: OBSTACLE: a difficulty stands in the path and must be faced before progress continues.
branches.cn: 阻碍：困难立在路上，必须先面对它，才能继续前进。

branches.en: DISCOVERY: a word in a text or a species in the field is simply something met along the way.
branches.cn: 发现：文本里的一个词、野外的一个物种，都只是路上碰到的东西。

branches.en: THERAPY: in the encounter group, facing another person openly is itself the treatment.
branches.cn: 治疗：在交心团体里，坦诚地面对另一个人，本身就是治疗。

intro.en: Encounter's family is built on Latin contra 'against'. Prefixes and compounds show whether the meeting is hostile, repeated, or therapeutic.
intro.cn: encounter 的词族建立在拉丁语 contra“对着”上。前缀与复合形式显示这次相遇是敌对的、重复的，还是治疗性的。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin layer is contra 'against' and Late Latin incontra 'in front of'. There is no classical Latin verb *encounter; the verb is French, which is why the Latin list stops at the prepositional forms.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁层是 contra“对着”与晚期拉丁语 incontra“在……前面”。古典拉丁语并没有 *encounter 这个动词；动词来自法语，因此拉丁词条只列介词性形式。

items.structure: Old French encontrer < Late Latin incontra
items.meaning: to meet, especially unexpectedly or as an opponent
items.meaningCN: 相遇，尤指意外地或作为对手相遇
items.example: We encountered the same problem twice.
items.exampleCN: 我们两次遇到同一个问题。

items.meaning: to oppose, reply to a blow with a blow
items.meaningCN: 反击；以一击回应一击（由 encounter 缩略）
items.example: The boxer countered with a short left hook.
items.exampleCN: 拳手用一记短左勾拳反击。

items.meaning: against, in opposition, as in counterargument
items.meaningCN: 反对、对抗，如 counterargument（反论点）（来自 contra 的前缀）
items.example: She wrote a counterargument to the editorial.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一篇反驳社论的文章。

items.meaning: a therapy group meeting for open emotional exchange
items.meaningCN: 以坦诚情感交流为目的的治疗团体（1967 年始见）
items.example: He joined an encounter group after the divorce.
items.exampleCN: 离婚后他加入了一个交心团体。

items.meaning: a very near meeting, especially with something unusual or alien
items.meaningCN: 极近距离的接触，尤指与不寻常之物或外星生命
items.example: The pilot reported a close encounter with an unknown object.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员报告与一个不明物体发生了近距离接触。

items.meaning: a meeting that happens by accident
items.meaningCN: 偶然发生的相遇
items.example: Their partnership began with a chance encounter in a lift.
items.exampleCN: 他们的合作始于电梯里的一次偶遇。

items.meaning: to meet or experience something again
items.meaningCN: 再次遇见或再次经历（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The book lets readers re-encounter the story as adults.
items.exampleCN: 这本书让读者成年后重遇这个故事。

items.meaning: a meeting or confrontation with a particular person or thing
items.meaningCN: 与特定人或物的相遇或对抗（with 标记对象）
items.example: His encounter with the law changed his career.
items.exampleCN: 他与法律的这次交锋改变了他的职业。

items.meaning: a scheduled meeting of an encounter group
items.meaningCN: 交心团体的一次定期活动
items.example: The encounter session lasted three hours.
items.exampleCN: 那次交心活动持续了三小时。

items.meaning: an attack made in response to an attack
items.meaningCN: 为回应进攻而发动的反攻（counter- 表示“反”）
items.example: The counterattack retook the hill before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 反攻在天亮前夺回了山头。

definition_zh: 能量；能源；精力；活力；劲头
definition_en: the capacity to do work or cause change, the power supplied as electricity or fuel, or the vigour a person or group has
core_image: 一团向内收着的劲：看着不动，一旦放开就能推动别的东西。
scene: The runners saved their energy for the final climb.
sceneCN: 这里 energy 是「人的体力、精力」（第 3 个义项：个人活力）；句意：跑者们把体力留到最后一段爬坡。场景要点：半山腰、放慢的脚步、水壶。

pos.zh: 能量；能源；精力；活力

derivatives.zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；高能的

senses.title: Physics: capacity to do work
senses.titleCN: 物理能量：做功的本领
senses.definition: the capacity of a body or system to do work or produce change, measured in joules
senses.definitionCN: 物体或系统做功或产生变化的本领，以焦耳计
senses.example: The falling water converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
senses.exampleCN: 落下的水把势能转化为动能。
senses.why: Greek energeia was Aristotle's word for 'activity, actuality' — being at work. Physics took the word for whatever can be put to work.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 energeia 是亚里士多德用来表示“活动、现实性”的词——正在起作用。物理学用它指“任何能被用来做功的东西”。

senses.title: Electricity supplied to users
senses.titleCN: 电力：送到用户家里的那部分
senses.definition: electricity as a supply that homes and industry consume
senses.definitionCN: 作为家庭与工业消耗的电力供应
senses.example: The town buys half its energy from a local wind farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇上一半的电力购自当地风电场。
senses.why: The abstract capacity becomes a commodity once it is metered and billed. Energy here is a quantity delivered through a wire.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计量、可以计费，抽象的本领就变成了商品。这里的 energy 是通过电线送来的一个量。

senses.title: A person's vigour
senses.titleCN: 人的精力：身体里的劲
senses.definition: the physical and mental strength that lets a person stay active
senses.definitionCN: 使人保持活动的体力与心力
senses.example: He had no energy left after the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班之后他一点力气都没有了。
senses.why: The body is treated as a system with a store of work-capacity. Spending it leaves less for the next task, exactly like a battery.
senses.whyCN: 身体被当成一个有做功存量的系统。用掉一些，下一件事就少一些，和电池一模一样。

senses.title: Force of expression
senses.titleCN: 语言的力量：表达的劲道
senses.definition: the force or vividness with which something is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 表达时所带的力度或生动性
senses.example: The speech lost its energy when the last paragraph was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 末段被删掉后，这篇演讲失去了劲道。
senses.why: This is the sense with which the word entered English in the 1590s: 'force of expression'. It came from a misreading of Aristotle's 'actuality'.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语时的意思：“表达的力量”。它来自对亚里士多德“现实性”的误读。

senses.title: The drive to act
senses.titleCN: 行动的劲头：愿意往前推
senses.definition: the motivation or drive that makes a person or group act
senses.definitionCN: 促使个人或群体行动的动机与冲劲
senses.example: The campaign ran on the energy of its volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动靠志愿者的干劲运转。
senses.why: Work-capacity becomes willingness. A group with energy is one that can keep exerting itself, so the physical store turns into social drive.
senses.whyCN: 做功的存量变成了意愿。有 energy 的群体，是能持续使力的群体，物理存量由此变成社会动力。

senses.title: Fuel and resources for power
senses.titleCN: 能源资源：可烧、可转换的料
senses.definition: natural resources such as oil, gas, coal, or sunlight used to produce power
senses.definitionCN: 用于产能的石油、天然气、煤、阳光等自然资源
senses.example: The country is rich in energy but poor in water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家能源丰富，却缺水。
senses.why: The resource is potential work stored in matter. Calling oil 'energy' is shorthand for 'material that can release energy'.
senses.whyCN: 资源就是储存在物质里的潜在做功能力。把石油叫作 energy，是“能释放能量的物质”的简称。

senses.title: Energy in food
senses.titleCN: 食物热量：吃进去的燃料
senses.definition: the amount of heat or fuel value that a food provides to the body
senses.definitionCN: 食物为身体提供的热量或燃料价值
senses.example: Nuts are dense in energy for their size.
senses.exampleCN: 坚果个头小，热量却很密集。
senses.why: The body is an engine; food is its fuel. The same word covers both because both are measured in the same units.
senses.whyCN: 身体是发动机，食物是燃料。同一个词覆盖两者，因为它们用同样的单位计量。

senses.title: Vitality of a place or scene
senses.titleCN: 场所的活力：人多、事多、劲足
senses.definition: the liveliness and activity that a place, market, or social scene has
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、市场或社交场面所具有的生气与活跃度
senses.example: The old port has a creative energy it lacked in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老港区有一种 1990 年代没有的创造活力。
senses.why: The metaphor widens again: a place is a system that can be more or less at work, and its visible activity is its energy.
senses.whyCN: 比喻再度扩大：一个地方是一个可多可少“在运转”的系统，它可见的活跃就是它的能量。

senses.title: Effort directed at a task
senses.titleCN: 投入的精力：把劲用在哪
senses.definition: the effort or attention that someone chooses to give to a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 某人选择投入某项活动的努力或注意力
senses.example: She put most of her energy into teaching rather than research.
senses.exampleCN: 她把大部分精力放在教学而不是研究上。
senses.why: Energy is finite, so putting it somewhere implies taking it from somewhere else. The word becomes a way of talking about allocation.
senses.whyCN: 能量有限，投到某处就意味着从别处拿走。这个词由此成了谈论“分配”的方式。

intro.en: Energy comes from Aristotle's Greek word for 'being at work'. It entered English meaning 'force of expression', turned into 'power' in the 17th century, and only became a scientific term in 1807.
intro.cn: energy 来自亚里士多德表示“正在起作用”的希腊词。它进入英语时意为“表达的力量”，17 世纪转为“力量”，直到 1807 年才成为科学术语。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed, action'. It goes back to PIE *werg- 'to do', the root behind English work and wright.
items.cn: ergon 意为“工作、行为、行动”。它上溯到原始印欧语 *werg-“做”，是英语 work 与 wright 的词根。

items.en: Energeia was 'activity, action, operation'. Aristotle used it for 'actuality, reality, existence', as opposed to potential.
items.cn: energeia 意为“活动、行动、运作”。亚里士多德用它表示“现实性、实在、存在”，与“潜能”相对。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek word but misread Aristotle's 'actuality' as 'force of expression' — the power that calls up realistic pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入了这个希腊词，却把亚里士多德的“现实性”误读为“表达的力量”——那种能在心里唤起逼真图景的力量。

items.en: French énergie carried the Latin sense into English. English records energy in the 1590s meaning 'force of expression'.
items.cn: 法语 énergie 把拉丁义带进英语。英语在 16 世纪 90 年代记录 energy，意为“表达的力量”。

items.en: The broader sense 'power' is first recorded in the 1660s. The scientific use, as a measurable quantity, dates from 1807.
items.cn: 较宽的“力量”义最早记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。作为可测量的量，科学用法始于 1807 年。

items.en: Energy crisis is attested from 1970. The word now covers electricity bills, gym sessions, and the mood of a city, all from one Greek verb for work.
items.cn: energy crisis 于 1970 年见于记录。这个词如今覆盖电费单、健身课与城市气氛，全都出自同一个表示“工作”的希腊动词。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek ergon 'work' root; the second collects words for power and vigour.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语 ergon“工作”词根；第二组收“力量与活力”类词。

entries.definition: full of energy; active and forceful. It adds -etic to the Greek stem, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛的；活跃有力的。它把 -etic 加在希腊词干上，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to give energy to something, or to supply electricity to a device
entries.definitionCN: 给某物能量；给设备通电（由 energy 派生）

entries.definition: extra effect produced by two things working together. Greek syn- 'together' + ergon 'work'.
entries.definitionCN: 两物协作产生的额外效果。希腊语 syn-“共同”+ ergon“工作”。

entries.definition: a small unit of energy in the centimetre-gram-second system, named directly from Greek ergon 'work'.
entries.definitionCN: 厘米-克-秒制中的小能量单位，直接由希腊语 ergon“工作”命名。

entries.definition: in physics, the rate at which energy is used; in daily life, electricity or influence. It is not the same quantity as energy.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上指能量被使用的速率；日常指电力或影响力。它与 energy 不是同一个量。

entries.definition: a push or pull that can change motion. Force acts on a body; energy is what the body has or transfers.
entries.definitionCN: 能改变运动的推或拉。力作用于物体；能量是物体拥有或转移的东西。

entries.definition: the quality of being alive and full of strength. It is close to energy in the personal sense but more about life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 有生命且充满力量的状态。它接近 energy 的个人义，但更关于“生命本身”。

entries.definition: strength and enthusiasm in action. It is more formal than energy and often about sustained effort.
entries.definitionCN: 行动中的力量与热情。它比 energy 正式，常指持续的用力。

entries.definition: the ability to keep going for a long time. It is energy measured over duration.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间坚持下去的能力。它可说是以“持续时间”计量的 energy。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek en 'at' + ergon 'work', giving energeia 'activity'; family words energetic, energize, energetics, synergy, erg, and the native English work from the same PIE root.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 en“在”+ ergon“工作”，合成 energeia“活动”；词族为 energetic、energize、energetics、synergy、erg，以及同源印欧词根的本土词 work。

normal.en: Ergon is 'work'; energy is the capacity for work, whichever form it is stored in.
normal.cn: ergon 是“工作”；energy 就是“做功的本领”，无论它以什么形式储存。

normal.en: Synergy is syn- 'together' + ergon: work that only happens when two things cooperate.
normal.cn: synergy 是 syn-“共同”+ ergon：只有两物协作才出现的工作效果。

normal.en: The word first meant 'force of expression' — a speech can have energy before a battery can.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指“表达的力量”——演讲能比电池更早有 energy。

normal.en: Power and energy are not the same: power is how fast energy is used.
normal.cn: power 与 energy 不同：power 是能量被使用的快慢。

normal.en: A food label in calories is an energy label, because the body is an engine.
normal.cn: 食品标签上的卡路里就是能量标签，因为身体是一台发动机。

abstract.en: Energy is the only currency every system accepts.
abstract.cn: 能量是唯一被所有系统接受的货币。

abstract.en: What you spend your energy on is the truest statement of what you value.
abstract.cn: 你把精力花在哪里，是对你在乎什么最真实的陈述。

abstract.en: Actuality is the old meaning: to have energy is to be, not merely to be able to be.
abstract.cn: actuality 是它古老的含义：有能量即是“在”，而不只是“可能在”。

examples.en: Solar panels turn sunlight into electrical energy.
examples.cn: 太阳能板把阳光转化为电能。

examples.en: She threw all her energy into getting the clinic reopened.
examples.cn: 她把全部精力投入到让诊所重新开张。

examples.en: The debate lost energy once the two main speakers left.
examples.cn: 两位主要发言人一走，辩论就失去了劲道。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摁呢挤”——把最后一点劲儿摁住、再挤出来，人还能往前推 → energy 能量、精力

root: 源自希腊语 energeia“活动、现实性”，由 en“在”+ ergon“工作”构成（ergon 上溯原始印欧语 *werg-“做”，与英语 work 同源）；经晚期拉丁语 energia、法语 énergie 进入英语，16 世纪 90 年代义为“表达的力量”，17 世纪 60 年代转为“力量”，1807 年成为科学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of energy, all one quantity: a store of capacity for work, appearing as electricity, fuel, vigour, or expressive force.
sensesIntro.cn: energy 的九个义项是同一个量：做功能力的储存，以电力、燃料、体力或表达力等形式出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compressed spring or a charged cell, quiet but holding a push inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：压紧的弹簧或充好电的电池，安静地收着一股推力。

branches.en: MEASURED: joules, barrels, and calories are three ways of counting the same capacity.
branches.cn: 可计量：焦耳、桶、卡路里，是同一个本领的三种数法。

branches.en: DELIVERED: electricity is energy turned into a billed commodity moving through a wire.
branches.cn: 已送达：电力是能量变成可计费的商品，沿电线流动。

branches.en: PERSONAL: a body, a will, and a schedule all run on a finite store that must be allocated.
branches.cn: 个人：身体、意志与日程都靠一个有限存量运转，必须分配。

branches.en: EXPRESSION: the oldest English sense, where a sentence carries force the way a battery carries charge.
branches.cn: 表达：英语中最古老的义项，一句话带着力量，就像电池带着电荷。

branches.en: PLACES: a city or market can be more or less at work, and we read its activity as energy.
branches.cn: 场所：城市或市场可多可少地“在运转”，我们把它可见的活跃读作 energy。

intro.en: Energy's family is Greek ergon 'work' dressed in English endings. Suffixes mark the adjective, the adverb, the verb, and the science; compounds name the industries built on the quantity.
intro.cn: energy 的词族是希腊语 ergon“工作”穿上英语词尾。后缀标记形容词、副词、动词与学科；复合词则命名建立在这个量上的产业。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are Greek energeia, energos, and ergon, borrowed into Late Latin as energia. Latin added no new root; it passed the Greek word on.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是希腊语 energeia、energos、ergon，以 energia 的形式借入晚期拉丁语。拉丁语没有新增词根，只是把这个希腊词传了下去。

items.meaning: full of energy; active
items.meaningCN: 精力充沛的；活跃的（-ic 构成形容词，17 世纪 50 年代始见）
items.example: She is an energetic campaigner.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位精力充沛的活动家。

items.meaning: in a forceful, active way
items.meaningCN: 有力地；精力充沛地（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: He argued energetically against the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他激烈地反对这个计划。

items.meaning: to give energy to; to power a device
items.meaningCN: 给……能量；给设备通电（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The speech energized the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲让整个团队振作起来。

items.meaning: the study of energy and its transformations
items.meaningCN: 研究能量及其转化的学科（-ics 构成学科名词）
items.example: The course begins with thermodynamics and energetics.
items.exampleCN: 这门课从热力学与能量学讲起。

items.meaning: something that gives energy, such as a tonic or a charger
items.meaningCN: 提供能量之物，如提神饮料或充电装置（-er 构成施事名词）
items.example: The charger is a fast energizer for the drone.
items.exampleCN: 这个充电器能快速给无人机补能。

items.meaning: combined effect greater than the sum of separate effects
items.meaningCN: 大于各部分单独效果之和的联合效应（同一 ergon 词根）
items.example: The merger promised synergy but delivered layoffs.
items.exampleCN: 合并承诺协同增效，结果却带来裁员。

items.meaning: a small unit of energy
items.meaningCN: 一个小能量单位（直接取自 ergon）
items.example: One joule equals ten million ergs.
items.exampleCN: 一焦耳等于一千万尔格。

items.meaning: using less energy for the same result
items.meaningCN: 以更少能量取得同样效果的
items.example: The new pumps are far more energy-efficient.
items.exampleCN: 新水泵的能效高得多。

items.meaning: requiring a large amount of energy to produce
items.meaningCN: 生产时需要大量能源的
items.example: Aluminium smelting is highly energy-intensive.
items.exampleCN: 铝冶炼是高度耗能的。

items.meaning: a severe shortage of fuel or power
items.meaningCN: 燃料或电力的严重短缺（1970 年始见）
items.example: The 1973 oil shock triggered a global energy crisis.
items.exampleCN: 1973 年石油冲击引发了全球能源危机。

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin borrowing of Greek energeia

definition_zh: 执行；强制执行；实施；迫使；加固
definition_en: to make a law or rule be obeyed, to force something to happen, or to give something strength
core_image: 把力气灌进一条规则里：规则不再只是纸上的字，而是能顶住人的东西。
scene: Parking rules are strictly enforced along this street.
sceneCN: 这里 enforce 是「使规则被遵守、执行」（第 1 个义项：执行法规）；句意：这条街上的停车规定执行得很严。场景要点：禁停牌、罚单、巡查的车。

pos.zh: 执行；强制实施；迫使；加固

derivatives.zh: 可执行的；可强制履行的

senses.title: Make a law be obeyed
senses.titleCN: 执法：让法律真正生效
senses.definition: to make people obey a law by using authority, police, or penalties
senses.definitionCN: 通过权威、警察或处罚使人遵守法律
senses.example: The city began enforcing the noise limits last month.
senses.exampleCN: 本市上个月开始执行噪音限制。
senses.why: The word is en- 'make, put in' + force, from Latin fortis 'strong'. To enforce a law is to put strength into it so that it can stand against resistance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 en-“使、放入”+ force（来自拉丁语 fortis“强”）。enforce 一条法律，就是给它灌入力气，让它顶得住抵抗。

senses.title: Impose a rule or requirement
senses.titleCN: 强制规定：不给例外
senses.definition: to make a rule or condition apply whether people agree or not
senses.definitionCN: 不管人们是否同意，都使某条规则或条件生效
senses.example: The landlord enforced a strict no-pets policy.
senses.exampleCN: 房东严格执行禁止养宠物的规定。
senses.why: A policy has no strength of its own; it is a sentence on paper. Enforcement is the strength added to that sentence.
senses.whyCN: 政策本身没有力气，只是纸上的一句话。执行就是给这句话加上力气。

senses.title: Uphold order in a place
senses.titleCN: 维持秩序：把乱压回去
senses.definition: to keep order or control in a place, often against disruption
senses.definitionCN: 在某地维持秩序或控制，通常针对扰乱
senses.example: Officers enforced calm at the entrance to the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 警员在体育场入口维持秩序。
senses.why: Order is a structure that collapses without pressure. Enforcing it is holding the structure up with force.
senses.whyCN: 秩序是一种没有压力就会塌的结构。执行秩序，就是用力把它撑住。

senses.title: Make a contract or right effective
senses.titleCN: 执行合同：让条款能兑现
senses.definition: in law, to make a contract, right, or judgment actually take effect
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上使合同、权利或判决真正生效
senses.example: The court enforced the arbitration award.
senses.exampleCN: 法院强制执行了仲裁裁决。
senses.why: A right that cannot be enforced is only a claim. Enforcement is what turns a promise into something with weight behind it.
senses.whyCN: 不能执行的权力只是主张。执行，正是把承诺变成背后有分量的东西。

senses.title: Historical: fortify or strengthen
senses.titleCN: 古义：加固、使坚固
senses.definition: in older usage, to strengthen a place, an argument, or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指加固某地、某个论证或某座结构
senses.example: The castle was enforced with a second wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城堡又加了一道墙来加固。
senses.why: This is the medieval sense and the most literal one: en- 'make' + force 'strength' = make strong. Law enforcement is a later specialization.
senses.whyCN: 这是中世纪义，也最字面：en-“使”+ force“力量”= 使坚固。执法义是后来分化出来的专门用法。

senses.title: Force an outcome to happen
senses.titleCN: 强行促成：把结果顶出来
senses.definition: to make something happen by pressure rather than by agreement
senses.definitionCN: 靠压力而不是靠共识使某事发生
senses.example: The chair enforced a vote before the opposition was ready.
senses.exampleCN: 主席在反对派准备好之前强行发起表决。
senses.why: Strength is applied to an event, not a rule. The earliest English sense was 'to drive by physical force', and this use keeps that drive.
senses.whyCN: 力量被施加在事件上，而不是规则上。英语最早的意思是“以体力驱动”，这个用法保留了那股驱动。

senses.title: Sports: apply the rules
senses.titleCN: 体育执法：按规则判罚
senses.definition: of a referee, to apply the rules of a game and punish breaches
senses.definitionCN: 指裁判执行比赛规则并处罚违规
senses.example: The referee enforced the new scrum rule consistently.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判一致地执行了新的争球规则。
senses.why: The referee is the person who gives the rulebook its force on the field, which is why officials are called enforcers.
senses.whyCN: 裁判就是在场上给规则本子注入力气的人，所以执法者也被叫作 enforcer。

senses.title: Impose one's will on others
senses.titleCN: 强加意志：让别人照办
senses.definition: to make others accept one's will or demands through pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过压力使别人接受自己的意志或要求
senses.example: He enforced his version of the story on the rest of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的版本强加给团队其余成员。
senses.why: The strength now belongs to a person rather than a rule. Enforcing one's will is making one's intention as hard to resist as a law.
senses.whyCN: 这里的力气属于人而非规则。把自己的意志 enforce 出去，就是让自己的意图像法律一样难以抵抗。

intro.en: Enforce is en- 'make' plus force, from Latin fortis 'strong'. Its oldest sense is 'strengthen'; only in the 1640s did it specialize into 'compel obedience to a law'.
intro.cn: enforce 是 en-“使”加 force，后者来自拉丁语 fortis“强”。它最早的意思是“加固”，直到 17 世纪 40 年代才专门化出“强制遵守法律”之义。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, mighty, firm, brave'. English fort and fortress come from the same word.
items.cn: fortis 意为“强的、有力的、坚固的、勇敢的”。英语 fort 与 fortress 同出此词。

items.en: The noun *fortia 'strength, force' was formed from the neuter plural of fortis. It gave French force and English force.
items.cn: 名词 *fortia“力量、强力”由 fortis 的中性复数构成，衍生出法语 force 与英语 force。

items.en: Old French enforcier (12c.) meant 'strengthen, reinforce; use force on; oppress; violate'. English could also have formed the verb natively from en- + force.
items.cn: 古法语 enforcier（12 世纪）意为“加强、增援；对……用强；压迫；侵犯”。英语也可能由 en- + force 本土构成该动词。

items.en: Enforcen is recorded in the mid-14th century meaning 'to drive by physical force; try, attempt; fortify a place', and by the late 14th century 'compel; strengthen'.
items.cn: enforcen 于 14 世纪中期见于记录，意为“以体力驱动；尝试；加固某地”；到 14 世纪晚期又有“强迫；加强”之义。

items.en: The sense 'compel obedience to' a law is attested from the 1640s. The legal meaning becomes dominant, and the older 'strengthen' sense survives mainly in reinforce.
items.cn: “强制遵守”法律的义项 1640 年代见于记录。法律义逐渐占主导，较早的“加固”义主要保留在 reinforce 中。

items.en: Law enforcement becomes a fixed phrase and a whole profession. Enforceable, enforcement, and enforcer all follow from the legal sense.
items.cn: law enforcement 成为固定短语与一整个职业。enforceable、enforcement、enforcer 都从法律义衍生。

note.en: The first group shares the fortis 'strong' root; the second collects verbs of putting a rule or decision into effect.
note.cn: 第一组共享 fortis“强”词根；第二组收“使规则或决定生效”类动词。

entries.definition: strength, or a push that changes motion. Enforce is en- 'make' plus this word: to put force into something.
entries.definitionCN: 力量，或改变运动的推力。enforce 是 en-“使”加这个词：把力量放进某物。

entries.definition: to make stronger, especially with more people or material. Re- 'again' + inforce, a variant of enforce; it keeps the old 'strengthen' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 加强，尤指增加人手或材料。re-“再次”+ inforce（enforce 的变体），保留了古老的“加固”义。

entries.definition: able to be enforced, especially of a contract or law. Recorded from the 1580s.
entries.definitionCN: 可被强制执行的，尤指合同或法律。16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。

entries.definition: a strong building for defence. It is the literal 'strong place' behind fortis.
entries.definitionCN: 用于防御的坚固建筑。它是 fortis 背后字面的“坚固之处”。

entries.definition: to carry out a plan or system. It is about making something work in practice, not about punishing breaches.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划或制度。它关于让某事在实践中运转，而不关于处罚违规。

entries.definition: to place a rule, tax, or burden on people. It creates the obligation; enforce makes it bite.
entries.definitionCN: 把规则、税负或负担加到别人身上。它创造义务；enforce 让义务真正咬人。

entries.definition: to support or confirm a law or decision, especially in court. It defends validity rather than applying penalties.
entries.definitionCN: 支持或确认法律、裁决，尤在法庭上。它捍卫有效性，而非施加处罚。

entries.definition: to put a rule or method into use in a particular case. It is broader and gentler than enforce.
entries.definitionCN: 在具体情形中使用规则或方法。它比 enforce 更宽、更温和。

entries.definition: to manage and carry out laws or justice. It focuses on the institutional process rather than on compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 管理与执行法律或司法。它关注制度过程，而非强制。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: en- 'make, put in' + force, from Latin fortis 'strong'; family words enforcement, enforceable, enforcer, reinforce, fort, fortress.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：en-“使、放入”+ force，源头是拉丁语 fortis“强”；词族为 enforcement、enforceable、enforcer、reinforce、fort、fortress。

normal.en: Force is 'strength'; enforce is putting strength into a rule so it can resist you.
normal.cn: force 是“力量”；enforce 就是把力量灌进规则，让它顶得住你。

normal.en: Fort, fortress, fortis, force, enforce, reinforce: all one family of 'strong'.
normal.cn: fort、fortress、fortis、force、enforce、reinforce：全是“强”这一族。

normal.en: The word is old enough to have meant 'strengthen a castle wall' before 'apply a law'.
normal.cn: 这个词老到先表示“加固城墙”，后才有“执行法律”。

normal.en: Reinforce is re- + inforce; reinforcements are literally strength sent again.
normal.cn: reinforce 是 re- + inforce；reinforcements 字面上就是“再一次送来的力量”。

normal.en: A referee enforces the rulebook: the official who turns paper into pressure.
normal.cn: 裁判 enforce 规则本：把纸变成压力的那个人。

abstract.en: A rule without enforcement is a wish with good grammar.
abstract.cn: 没有执行的规则，只是一个语法通顺的愿望。

abstract.en: Enforcement is where a society decides how much of its ideal it will actually pay for.
abstract.cn: 执行，是社会决定自己究竟愿意为理想付多少钱的地方。

abstract.en: Every enforcement carries a question: whose strength, and against whom.
abstract.cn: 每一次强制执行都带着一个问题：谁的力量，对着谁。

examples.en: The agency lacks the staff to enforce the new safety rules.
examples.cn: 该机构缺少人手来执行新的安全规定。

examples.en: The treaty is technically valid but hard to enforce.
examples.cn: 这份条约在技术上有效，却难以强制执行。

examples.en: Local police enforced a curfew after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后，当地警方执行了宵禁。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因佛寺”——因佛寺规矩极严，谁犯规就被请出门 → enforce 执行、强制

root: 由 en-“使、放入”+ force 构成；force 来自俗拉丁语 *fortia，再上溯拉丁语 fortis“强的、坚固的”。字面是“把力量放进某物”，故最早义为“加固、加强”，14 世纪有“以力驱动”，17 世纪 40 年代才专指“强制遵守法律”。同族有 fort、fortress、reinforce。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of enforce, all one act: strength is put into a rule, an order, or a will so that resistance cannot simply ignore it.
sensesIntro.cn: enforce 的八个义项是同一个动作：把力量灌进一条规则、一道命令或一个意志，使抵抗无法轻易无视它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing down on a sheet of rules until the paper becomes a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在写满规则的纸上，直到纸变成一堵墙。

branches.en: RULES: laws, policies, and game rules all need an outside force to become real.
branches.cn: 规则：法律、政策与比赛规则，都需要一个外部力量才能变成现实。

branches.en: STRENGTH: in law, a right or contract is only real once a court can put weight behind it.
branches.cn: 强度：在法律上，权利或合同只有在法院能给它加上分量之后才算真实。

branches.en: SURVIVAL: the old 'strengthen' sense lives on in reinforce, where extra strength is sent again.
branches.cn: 遗存：古老的“加固”义活在 reinforce 里，那里是“再一次送来的力量”。

branches.en: PRESSURE: order and a forced outcome are both gaps where something must be held up by strength.
branches.cn: 压力：秩序与被强行促成的结果，都是必须有力量撑住的地方。

branches.en: WILL: a person can apply to an intention the same hardness a state applies to a law.
branches.cn: 意志：一个人可以把国家施加于法律的硬度，施加于自己的意图。

intro.en: Enforce's family is built on Latin fortis 'strong'. Suffixes mark the act, the possibility, and the person; the compounds belong to law and policing.
intro.cn: enforce 的词族建立在拉丁语 fortis“强”上。后缀标记行为、可能性与人；复合词则属于法律与治安领域。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are fortis 'strong' and the Vulgar Latin noun *fortia 'strength', which yields force. There is no classical Latin verb enforce; the verb is French or native English.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 fortis“强”与俗拉丁语名词 *fortia“力量”，后者衍生出 force。古典拉丁语没有 enforce 这个动词；它是法语或英语本土构成的。

items.meaning: the act of making a law or rule be obeyed
items.meaningCN: 使法律或规则被遵守的行为（-ment 构成行为名词）
items.example: Enforcement of the ban began in March.
items.exampleCN: 禁令的执行从三月开始。

items.meaning: able to be enforced in law
items.meaningCN: 在法律上可强制执行的（-able 构成能力形容词，16 世纪 80 年代始见）
items.example: The clause is not enforceable in this country.
items.exampleCN: 该条款在这个国家无法强制执行。

items.meaning: the quality of being enforceable
items.meaningCN: 可强制执行的性质（-ity 构成状态名词，1851 年始见）
items.example: The court questioned the enforceability of the agreement.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑该协议的可执行性。

items.meaning: one who enforces rules, often by force
items.meaningCN: 执行规则者，常靠强力（-er 构成施事名词）
items.example: He acted as the group's enforcer.
items.exampleCN: 他充当这个群体的执法者。

items.meaning: that cannot be enforced
items.meaningCN: 无法强制执行的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: A promise without a witness may be unenforceable.
items.exampleCN: 没有见证人的承诺可能无法强制执行。

items.meaning: to strengthen with more force, people, or material
items.meaningCN: 以更多力量、人手或材料加强（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: Steel bars reinforce the concrete.
items.exampleCN: 钢筋加固混凝土。

items.meaning: to enforce again, or to reinforce
items.meaningCN: 再次执行；或加强（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The city re-enforced the parking ban.
items.exampleCN: 市里再次执行了停车禁令。

items.meaning: the police and the system that makes laws be obeyed
items.meaningCN: 警察部门及使法律被遵守的体系
items.example: Law enforcement interviewed the witnesses.
items.exampleCN: 执法部门询问了证人。

items.meaning: an official step taken to compel compliance
items.meaningCN: 为强制合规而采取的官方行动
items.example: The regulator announced enforcement action against the firm.
items.exampleCN: 监管机构宣布对该公司采取执法行动。

items.meaning: working without an outside authority to enforce it
items.meaningCN: 无需外部权威执行即可自行生效的
items.example: The protocol is largely self-enforcing.
items.exampleCN: 这套协议在很大程度上自执行。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 强的；有力的；坚固的；勇敢的

latinEntries.structure: Vulgar Latin noun from neuter plural of fortis

definition_zh: 提高；增强；改善；美化；增值
definition_en: to increase or improve the quality, value, or attractiveness of something
core_image: 把一件东西从原来的高度再往上抬一截。
scene: A little salt enhances the flavour of the tomatoes.
sceneCN: 这里 enhance 是「提升某物的品质或效果」（第 1 个义项：提升品质）；句意：一点盐就能提升番茄的风味。场景要点：切开的番茄、指尖的盐、尝味的小勺。

pos.zh: 提高；增强；改善；美化

senses.title: Improve quality or value
senses.titleCN: 提升品质：把档次抬上去
senses.definition: to make the quality or value of something better
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的品质或价值变得更好
senses.example: Good lighting enhances the quality of the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 好的光线提升了照片的质量。
senses.why: Enhance comes from Latin altus 'high', literally 'grown tall'. To enhance is to raise a thing to a higher level, and the level here is quality.
senses.whyCN: enhance 来自拉丁语 altus“高”，字面是“长高了”。enhance 就是把某物抬到更高的层级，这里的层级是品质。

senses.title: Make something more attractive
senses.titleCN: 美化：让外观更抓眼
senses.definition: to make a place, object, or person look better or more appealing
senses.definitionCN: 使地点、物体或人看起来更好、更有吸引力
senses.example: The garden enhances the front of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园美化了房子的正面。
senses.why: The raised thing is now appearance. Height becomes beauty because both are read as 'more' of a good quality.
senses.whyCN: 被抬高的是外观。高度变成美感，因为二者都被读作“某种好品质的更多”。

senses.title: Strengthen a skill or ability
senses.titleCN: 增强能力：把水平提上去
senses.definition: to make a skill, capacity, or function stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使某项技能、能力或功能更强、更有效
senses.example: The course enhances students' ability to argue in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课增强了学生的书面论证能力。
senses.why: Ability can be pictured as a level; training raises it. The Latin 'make high' applies to anything that can be measured by degree.
senses.whyCN: 能力可以被想象成一个水平面；训练把它抬高。拉丁语的“使高”适用于任何能按程度衡量的东西。

senses.title: Increase intensity or effect
senses.titleCN: 增强效果：让作用更明显
senses.definition: to make the effect of something stronger or more noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的作用更强或更明显
senses.example: The fog enhanced the red of the lighthouse lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 雾气使灯塔的红色灯光更醒目。
senses.why: Here the raised quantity is intensity. The image is no longer a physical height but a dial turned up.
senses.whyCN: 这里被抬高的量是强度。意象不再是物理高度，而是一个被调高的旋钮。

senses.title: Raise status or reputation
senses.titleCN: 提升声望：把位置往上挪
senses.definition: to increase someone's standing, reputation, or position
senses.definitionCN: 提高某人的地位、声望或位置
senses.example: The award enhanced his reputation among critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项提高了他在评论界的声望。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense in English, from about 1300: 'raise in station, wealth, or fame'. Social height is literal height.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早记录的义项，约 1300 年：“提高地位、财富或声望”。社会高度就是字面的高度。

senses.title: Digital: improve an image
senses.titleCN: 图像增强：把细节提出来
senses.definition: to improve the clarity, contrast, or resolution of an image or recording
senses.definitionCN: 提高图像或录音的清晰度、对比度或分辨率
senses.example: The software enhances old photographs without smoothing faces.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件能增强老照片，又不会把脸磨平。
senses.why: The picture is lifted toward a clearer version of itself. Enhancement implies adding what was already latent, not inventing it.
senses.whyCN: 照片被抬向一个更清晰的自己。增强意味着把本来潜藏的东西提出来，而不是编造。

senses.title: Add to the appeal of a product
senses.titleCN: 增值：让商品更想被买
senses.definition: to increase the attractiveness or selling power of a product or offer
senses.definitionCN: 提高产品或方案吸引力与销售力
senses.example: A free trial enhances the appeal of the subscription.
senses.exampleCN: 免费试用提升了订阅的吸引力。
senses.why: Value is treated as a height on a scale. Adding a benefit moves the product up that scale.
senses.whyCN: 价值被当作刻度上的高度。增加一项好处，就是把产品往那根刻度上推。

senses.title: Bring out a flavour
senses.titleCN: 提味：让味道更突出
senses.definition: to make the taste of food more vivid or complete
senses.definitionCN: 使食物的味道更鲜明或更完整
senses.example: A squeeze of lemon enhances the sweetness of the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 挤一点柠檬能提升鱼的鲜甜。
senses.why: The flavour was there but low; the added element raises it above the other tastes. Even cooking uses the 'lift' image.
senses.whyCN: 味道本来在，只是低；加入的那一点把它抬到其他味道之上。连烹饪也用“抬高”的意象。

intro.en: Enhance goes back to Latin altus 'high', literally 'grown tall'. The path runs through Old French and Anglo-French, and the spelling with -h- and -n- is explained only as probable influence.
intro.cn: enhance 上溯到拉丁语 altus“高”，字面是“长高了”。它经古法语与盎格鲁-法语传入英语；其中 -h- 与 -n- 的来历只能解释为“很可能的影响”。

items.en: The root *al- meant 'to grow, nourish'. It also gives Latin alere 'to feed' and English old, adult, and alumnus.
items.cn: 词根 *al- 意为“生长、养育”。它还衍生出拉丁语 alere“喂养”以及英语 old、adult、alumnus。

items.en: Altus meant 'high', literally 'grown tall', from the same root as alere. Height in Latin is something that has grown.
items.cn: altus 意为“高的”，字面是“已长高的”，与 alere 同根。拉丁语里的高度，是“已经长起来”的东西。

items.en: Inaltare meant 'to raise, exalt', from in- + altare 'make high' from altus. Vulgar Latin *inaltiare carries it toward French.
items.cn: inaltare 意为“举起、抬高”，由 in- + 来自 altus 的 altare“使高”构成。俗拉丁语 *inaltiare 把它带向法语。

items.en: Enhaucier meant 'make greater, make higher or louder; fatten, foster; raise in esteem'. The -h- is supposedly from Frankish *hoh 'high'.
items.cn: enhaucier 意为“使更大、更高或更响；养肥、培育；提高评价”。其中的 -h- 据说是受法兰克语 *hoh“高”的影响。

items.en: Anglo-French enhauncer is the immediate source of English. The -n- is perhaps due to Provençal enansar 'promote', from Latin in + ante 'before'.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 enhauncer 是英语的直接来源。其中的 -n- 也许来自普罗旺斯语 enansar“促进”，后者由拉丁语 in + ante“在前”构成。

items.en: English records anhaunsen in the late 13th century meaning 'to raise, make higher', and by about 1300 'raise in station, wealth, or fame'. The modern spellings settle later.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪晚期记录 anhaunsen，意为“举起、使更高”；约 1300 年有“提高地位、财富或声望”。现代拼写更晚才固定。

note.en: The first group is the enhancement family plus one common spelling trap; the second collects verbs of making something better.
note.cn: 第一组是 enhancement 词族，外加一个常见的拼写陷阱；第二组收“使某物更好”的动词。

entries.definition: the act or result of improving something. Recorded from the 1570s, from enhance + -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 改善某物的行为或结果。16 世纪 70 年代见于记录，由 enhance + -ment 构成。

entries.definition: something that enhances, such as a flavour enhancer or an image enhancer
entries.definitionCN: 起增强作用的东西，如增味剂或图像增强器

entries.definition: to charm or delight; historically to put under a spell. It comes from Latin incantare 'sing onto', not from altus 'high'.
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷；历史上指施魔法。它来自拉丁语 incantare“对着唱”，与 altus“高”无关。

entries.definition: to make stronger or more intense. It uses the native English height, but the metaphor is identical to enhance.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强或更强烈。它用英语本土的 height，但比喻与 enhance 完全一致。

entries.definition: to make or become better. It is the broad neutral word; enhance usually implies adding a quality rather than fixing a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 使变得更好。它是最宽的中性词；enhance 通常指增加某种品质，而非修补缺陷。

entries.definition: to raise or increase something, often quickly. It is more informal and often about numbers or morale.
entries.definitionCN: 提高或增加某物，常较迅速。它更口语，多用于数字或士气。

entries.definition: to add to something to make it larger or more effective. It stresses addition; enhance stresses raised quality.
entries.definitionCN: 增添以使其更大或更有效。它强调“增加”，enhance 强调“品质被抬高”。

entries.definition: to replace something with a better version. It often means substitution, where enhance means improving what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 用更好的版本替换。它常指替换，而 enhance 指改善已有的东西。

entries.definition: to make a feeling or effect stronger. It is closest to enhance in the 'increase intensity' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使感觉或效果更强。它在“增强强度”义上与 enhance 最接近。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin altus 'high', literally 'grown tall', from PIE *al- 'grow'; through Old French enhaucier and Anglo-French enhauncer; family words enhancement, enhancer, enhanced, and the native heighten.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 altus“高”，字面“已长高”，源自原始印欧语 *al-“生长”；经古法语 enhaucier 与盎格鲁-法语 enhauncer 传入；词族为 enhancement、enhancer、enhanced，以及本土词 heighten。

normal.en: The Latin base is altus 'high': to enhance is to raise something on a scale.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基是 altus“高”：enhance 就是把某物在刻度上抬高。

normal.en: Altitude, altimeter, exalt, enhance: all the same 'high' family.
normal.cn: altitude、altimeter、exalt、enhance：全是同一个“高”的家族。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was social: to raise a person's station or fame.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义是社会性的：提高一个人的地位或声望。

normal.en: An enhancer does not create the flavour; it lifts what was already there.
normal.cn: 增味剂并不创造味道；它只是把本来就在的味道抬起来。

normal.en: Heighten is the native twin of enhance, built on the same height metaphor.
normal.cn: heighten 是 enhance 的本土孪生词，建立在同一个“高度”比喻上。

abstract.en: Enhancement is the art of making something more itself.
abstract.cn: 增强，是让某物“更像它自己”的手艺。

abstract.en: Every scale we enhance on was chosen by someone.
abstract.cn: 我们用来“提升”的每一根刻度，都是有人选定的。

abstract.en: To raise one quality is usually to let another fall out of view.
abstract.cn: 抬高一种品质，通常就是让另一种品质退出视野。

examples.en: The new windows enhance both the light and the sound insulation.
examples.cn: 新窗户既改善了采光，也提升了隔音。

examples.en: Nothing enhances a room like a single well-placed lamp.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一盏位置得当的灯更能提升房间的气质。

examples.en: The filter enhances contrast without changing the colours.
examples.cn: 这个滤镜增强对比度，而不改变颜色。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摁汉子”——把汉子摁在肩上往上举，让他站得更高 → enhance 提高、增强

root: 源自古法语 enhaucier / 盎格鲁-法语 enhauncer，上溯俗拉丁语 *inaltiare、晚期拉丁语 inaltare“举起、抬高”，词基是拉丁语 altus“高的”，字面“已长高”，源自原始印欧语 *al-“生长、养育”（与 alere“喂养”、adult、old 同源）。核心是“把某物在刻度上抬高”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of enhance, all one movement: put something at a higher point on whatever scale measures it — quality, beauty, strength, status, or clarity.
sensesIntro.cn: enhance 的八个义项是同一个动作：把某物放到衡量它的那根刻度上更高的位置——品质、美感、强度、地位或清晰度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting an object one notch higher on a marked scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一件东西在有刻度的尺子上抬高了一格。

branches.en: QUALITY: craft lifts a thing on the scale of how well it is made.
branches.cn: 品质：工艺把一件东西在“做得多好”这根刻度上抬高。

branches.en: ABILITY: training raises a person's level, one notch at a time.
branches.cn: 能力：训练一次一格地抬高一个人的水平。

branches.en: SENSES: appearance and flavour are read as richer or fuller when the right element is added.
branches.cn: 感官：加入恰当的元素后，外观与味道被读作更丰富、更饱满。

branches.en: INTENSITY: a dial turned up and a photo made clearer are the same 'more' applied to effect and detail.
branches.cn: 强度：调高的旋钮与变清晰的照片，都是把“更多”用在效果与细节上。

branches.en: VALUE: status and selling power are heights on a social or market scale.
branches.cn: 价值：地位与卖点，是社会或市场刻度上的高度。

intro.en: Enhance's family is small and English-made on a Latin base. The suffixes mark the act, the result, and the thing that does the lifting; compounds come from imaging and food.
intro.cn: enhance 的词族很小，是在拉丁词基上由英语构成。后缀标记行为、结果与“执行抬升”的东西；复合词来自影像与食品领域。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are altus 'high', altare 'make high', and inaltare 'raise'. Vulgar Latin *inaltiare is reconstructed rather than attested, and the -h- and -n- in French are explained only as probable influences.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 altus“高”、altare“使高”与 inaltare“举起”。俗拉丁语 *inaltiare 是重构形式而非有文献实证；法语中的 -h- 与 -n- 只能解释为“很可能”的影响。

items.meaning: to raise the quality or value of something
items.meaningCN: 提高某物的品质或价值（en- 表“使”，词基为 altus“高”）
items.example: Soft light enhances the stone.
items.exampleCN: 柔和的光线提升了石头的质感。

items.meaning: an improvement or the act of improving
items.meaningCN: 改善；改善的行为或结果（-ment 构成名词，16 世纪 70 年代始见）
items.example: The update is a modest enhancement, not a redesign.
items.exampleCN: 这次更新只是小幅增强，不是重做。

items.meaning: improved or made stronger
items.meaningCN: 已增强的；被提高的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: The app offers enhanced privacy controls.
items.exampleCN: 这款应用提供增强的隐私控制。

items.meaning: a substance or device that enhances something
items.meaningCN: 增强某物的物质或装置（-er 构成施事名词）
items.example: MSG is a common flavour enhancer.
items.exampleCN: 味精是一种常见的增味剂。

items.meaning: having the effect of improving something
items.meaningCN: 具有增强作用的（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: It is a mood-enhancing drug.
items.exampleCN: 这是一种改善情绪的药物。

items.meaning: the act of making oneself look or feel better, especially in psychology
items.meaningCN: 自我提升；心理学中指让自己显得或感觉更好
items.example: Self-enhancement bias affects how people rate their skills.
items.exampleCN: 自我提升偏差会影响人们对自己技能的评价。

items.meaning: the process of improving a picture's clarity or contrast
items.meaningCN: 改善图像清晰度或对比度的过程
items.example: Image enhancement revealed a faint signature.
items.exampleCN: 图像增强显示出一个模糊的签名。

items.meaning: the improvement of an athlete's or system's output
items.meaningCN: 运动员或系统输出的提升
items.example: The rules ban most forms of performance enhancement.
items.exampleCN: 规则禁止大多数形式的成绩增强手段。

items.meaning: a substance added to make food taste fuller
items.meaningCN: 为使食物味道更饱满而添加的物质
items.example: The label lists no flavour enhancers.
items.exampleCN: 标签上没有列出任何增味剂。

items.meaning: to make something more attractive or persuasive
items.meaningCN: 使某物更有吸引力或说服力（固定搭配）
items.example: A short sample enhances the appeal of the course.
items.exampleCN: 一小段样课提升了这门课的吸引力。
